## P3 - `nokia_srsim` distributed nodes lack the same pre-holder compatibility fallback as `srl`

**Location:** [nodes/sros/sros.go:1819-1842](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/nodes/sros/sros.go#L1819-L1842)

**Problem:** This PR adds the `deployedWithoutNetnsNode` fallback so SR Linux nodes deployed before the netns holder keep working, but the sibling kind `nokia_srsim` shares the same holder lifecycle without an equivalent. In `sros.Start`, the distributed-base path calls `n.netnsNode.EnsureRunning(ctx, n.Cfg.ShortName)` unconditionally &#40;[`nodes/sros/sros.go:1827`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/nodes/sros/sros.go#L1827-L1827)&#41;, and `sros.GetNSPath` returns `n.netnsNode.GetNSPath(ctx)` for distributed base nodes &#40;[`nodes/sros/netns.go:90`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/nodes/sros/netns.go#L90-L90)&#41; with no fallback. The holder was introduced for srsim earlier by the &#34;SR-SIM netns ownership&#34; change documented in [`docs/rn/0.80.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/docs/rn/0.80.md#L1-L1).

**Trigger:** A distributed `nokia_srsim` lab deployed by a pre-0.80 containerlab &#40;before the srsim netns holder&#41; is managed with `clab start`, a stop/`start` cycle, `tools netem`, or link operations by a binary including this PR. `EnsureRunning` fails with the &#34;not found; recreate the node&#34; error and `GetNSPath` errors, which is the same class of failure the PR fixes for `nokia_srlinux`.

**Impact:** The stated compatibility goal is only fulfilled for one of the two kinds that use the netns holder; users of distributed srsim labs keep hitting `start` failures that the same fix pattern would resolve. One caveat&#58; the pre-0.80 srsim netns ownership shape &#40;which container owned the netns&#41; could not be verified from this snapshot, so the fallback target should be confirmed before porting.

**Suggested correction:** Extract the fallback into a shared helper on `NetnsHolder` &#40;for example `DeployedWithoutHolder(ctx) bool`&#41; and use it in both `srl.Start`/`srl.GetNSPath` and the sros distributed-base paths in `sros.Start` and `sros.GetNSPath`. If the legacy srsim netns shape turns out to differ, document why sros is excluded so the kinds stay consistent.


## P4 - Garbled comment on `deployedWithoutNetnsNode`; helper is not nil-safe

**Location:** [nodes/srl/netns.go:117-123](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/nodes/srl/netns.go#L117-L123)

**Problem:** The comment &#34;it keeps its own network namespace, as a node deployed by a containerlab before the holder does until it is recreated&#34; is grammatically broken and hard to parse. Additionally, the helper dereferences `n.netnsNode` without a nil guard; both current call sites &#40;[`srl.go:421`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/nodes/srl/srl.go#L421-L421) and `netns.go:127`&#41; only avoid a panic through `\|\|` short-circuiting.

**Trigger:** A future maintainer reads the helper to understand the compatibility heuristic, or adds a new call site without repeating the nil guard.

**Impact:** Misleading documentation on a load-bearing predicate and a latent nil-pointer hazard for future callers.

**Suggested correction:** Rewrite the comment, for example&#58; &#34;reports whether the node keeps its own network namespace&#58; the holder container is missing while the node container still exists, which happens for nodes deployed by a containerlab version before the netns holder; such nodes keep working until they are recreated.&#34; Optionally return `false` when `n.netnsNode == nil` inside the helper so it is safe to call unconditionally.


## P4 - Fallback masks the actionable &#34;recreate the node&#34; error when the holder was removed while the node is stopped

**Location:** [nodes/srl/srl.go:420-434](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/nodes/srl/srl.go#L420-L434)

**Problem:** The status-based heuristic in `deployedWithoutNetnsNode` cannot distinguish a legacy node with its own netns from a holder-model node whose holder container was deleted. In the latter case with the node stopped, the fallback enters `DefaultNode.Start` and calls `StartContainer` on a container whose `NetworkMode` is `container:<holder>` &#40;[`nodes/srl/netns.go:96`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/nodes/srl/netns.go#L96-L96)&#41; with the donor gone. This is inferred from Docker semantics, not measured, but the `start` is expected to fail with a low-level runtime error instead of the actionable message from `EnsureRunning` &#40;&#34;not found; recreate the node&#34;, [`nodes/netns_holder.go:41-45`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/nodes/netns_holder.go#L41-L45)&#41;.

**Trigger:** The internal `<node>-netns` container is removed manually or by external cleanup while the SR Linux container is stopped, followed by `clab start` or `apply`.

**Impact:** The operation still fails as before, but the error regresses from an explicit &#34;recreate the node&#34; instruction to a cryptic runtime error. For the running-node case the fallback is a strict improvement, so only the stopped-case diagnosability is affected.

**Suggested correction:** In the fallback path, when the node is not already running, log a warning &#40;or wrap the `DefaultNode.Start` error&#41; noting that the holder is not being used and that the node may need to be recreated if it was originally deployed with the netns holder.


## P4 - New backward-compatibility behavior is absent from the release notes

**Location:** [docs/rn/0.83.md:140-145](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/docs/rn/0.83.md#L140-L145)

**Problem:** The `0.83` release notes describe the netns holder &#40;[`docs/rn/0.83.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/docs/rn/0.83.md#L1-L1), &#34;Each `nokia_srlinux` node uses an internal `<node-name>-netns` holder container…&#34;&#41; but do not mention that nodes deployed by earlier releases keep working until recreated. Per the repository&#39;s release-note review rule, a user-visible behavior change such as this one &#40;labs that previously errored on `start` now work&#41; belongs in `docs/rn/`.

**Trigger:** A user reads the release notes for the holder feature to learn whether upgrading to it requires recreating existing SR Linux nodes.

**Impact:** The migration story is incomplete&#58; users cannot tell from the documentation that pre-holder deployments are tolerated and that the holder appears when the node is next recreated.

**Suggested correction:** Add one sentence to the holder section of the current in-development release note &#40;or the next release note if `0.83` is already published&#41;, for example&#58; &#34;SR Linux nodes deployed by earlier releases keep working without a holder; the holder is created when the node is next recreated.&#34;


## Coverage

- All three changed paths &#40;[`nodes/srl/netns.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/nodes/srl/netns.go#L1-L1), [`nodes/srl/srl.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/nodes/srl/srl.go#L1-L1), [`nodes/srl/netns_test.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/nodes/srl/netns_test.go#L1-L1)&#41; were reviewed in full, plus the base version of `netns.go` to confirm the minimal diff.
- Consumers of the changed methods were traced&#58; `DefaultNode.AddContainerNet` and `ExecFunction` &#40;[`nodes/default_node.go:961`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/nodes/default_node.go#L961-L961),999`), `clab tools netem&#96; &#40;[`cmd/tools_netem.go:261`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/cmd/tools_netem.go#L261-L261),548`), and the `apply&#96;/deploy reconcile flow &#40;[`core/topology_reconcile.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/core/topology_reconcile.go#L1-L1), [`core/deploy.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/core/deploy.go#L1-L1)&#41;, confirming an unchanged legacy node is not recreated and link operations use the fallback correctly.
- Runtime semantics verified by source&#58; docker `GetContainerStatus` swallows inspect errors into `NotFound` &#40;[`runtime/docker/docker.go:1942-1949`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/runtime/docker/docker.go#L1942-L1949)&#41;, `DefaultNode.Delete` tolerates `NotFound`, and `postStartActions` refreshes the netns symlink on every `start` &#40;[`runtime/docker/docker.go:1439-1451`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/runtime/docker/docker.go#L1439-L1451)&#41;.
- No topology/schema changes were made, so [`clab.schema.json`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/schemas/clab.schema.json#L1-L1) was not affected; the only docs gap is the release-note entry in finding 4.
- Tests were not executed &#40;read-only snapshot, execution not permitted&#41;; the three added tests were reviewed by inspection and look sound, though the holder-deleted-while-node-stopped case from finding 3 is untested.
- Unresolved uncertainties&#58; the exact Docker error when starting a container whose netns donor was removed &#40;inference, finding 3&#41;, and the pre-0.80 srsim netns ownership shape &#40;finding 1&#41;; both should be verified before acting on the suggestions.
- Normal-path performance&#58; the fallback probe adds one extra container inspect per `GetNSPath`/`Start` call &#40;holder status only; the node status is inspected only when the holder is missing&#41;. This is a cheap local API call and was not raised as a finding.

1: ---
2: description: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
3: alwaysApply: true
4: ---
5: 
6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```
70: 
71: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

(End of file - total 75 lines)
</content>

1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

15: const netnsNodeType = "srl-netns"
16: 
17: // usesNetnsNode reports whether the node runs in the network namespace of a holder container.
18: // Nodes with a user-defined network mode keep the network namespace of their own container.
19: func (n *srl) usesNetnsNode() bool {
20: 	return n.Cfg.NetworkMode == "" && !n.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased
21: }
22: 
23: func (n *srl) initNetnsNode() error {
24: 	if !n.usesNetnsNode() {
25: 		return nil
26: 	}
27: 
28: 	n.netnsNode = new(clabnodes.NetnsHolder)
29: 
30: 	return n.netnsNode.Init(n.newNetnsConfig(), clabnodes.WithRuntime(n.GetRuntime()))
31: }
32: 
33: func (n *srl) newNetnsConfig() *clabtypes.NodeConfig {
34: 	labels := maps.Clone(n.Cfg.Labels)
35: 
36: 	if labels == nil {
37: 		labels = map[string]string{}
38: 	}
39: 
40: 	shortName := n.Cfg.ShortName + "-netns"
41: 	labels[clabconstants.NodeName] = shortName
42: 
43: 	longName := n.Cfg.LongName + "-netns"
44: 	labels[clabconstants.LongName] = longName
45: 
46: 	labels[clabconstants.NodeType] = netnsNodeType
47: 	labels[clabconstants.InternalNode] = "true"
48: 
49: 	labels[clabconstants.RootNodeName] = n.Cfg.ShortName
50: 	labels[clabconstants.RootNodeLongName] = n.Cfg.LongName
51: 
52: 	return &clabtypes.NodeConfig{
53: 		ShortName:             shortName,
54: 		LongName:              longName,
55: 		Hostname:              n.Cfg.GetHostname(),
56: 		Fqdn:                  n.Cfg.Fqdn,

59: 		Kind:                  n.Cfg.Kind,
60: 		NodeType:              netnsNodeType,

91: // containerConfig returns the config of the SR Linux container attached to the holder's
92: // network namespace. The runtime rejects network settings for such containers, as they
93: // belong to the holder.
94: func (n *srl) containerConfig() *clabtypes.NodeConfig {
95: 	cfg := *n.Cfg
96: 	cfg.NetworkMode = "container:" + n.netnsNode.GetShortName()
97: 	cfg.DNS = nil
98: 	cfg.ExtraHosts = nil
99: 	cfg.MacAddress = ""
100: 	cfg.PortBindings = nil
101: 	cfg.PortSet = nil
102: 
103: 	return &cfg
104: }
105: 
106: // linkNetns points the node's netns symlink to the holder, as the namespace path of the
107: // SR Linux container changes whenever the container restarts.
108: func (n *srl) linkNetns(ctx context.Context) error {
109: 	nsPath, err := n.netnsNode.GetNSPath(ctx)
110: 	if err != nil {
111: 		return err
112: 	}
113: 
114: 	return clabutils.LinkContainerNS(nsPath, n.Cfg.LongName)
115: }
116: 
117: // deployedWithoutNetnsNode reports whether the node's container runs without a holder: it keeps
118: // its own network namespace, as a node deployed by a containerlab before the holder does until
119: // it is recreated.
120: func (n *srl) deployedWithoutNetnsNode(ctx context.Context) bool {
121: 	return n.netnsNode.GetContainerStatus(ctx) == clabruntime.NotFound &&
122: 		n.GetContainerStatus(ctx) != clabruntime.NotFound
123: }
124: 
125: // GetNSPath retrieves the Namespace Path.
126: func (n *srl) GetNSPath(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
127: 	if n.netnsNode == nil || n.deployedWithoutNetnsNode(ctx) {
128: 		return n.DefaultNode.GetNSPath(ctx)
129: 	}
130: 
131: 	return n.netnsNode.GetNSPath(ctx)
132: }
133: 
134: // DeleteNetnsSymlink deletes the symlink file created for the container netns.
135: func (n *srl) DeleteNetnsSymlink() error {
136: 	if n.netnsNode == nil {
137: 		return n.DefaultNode.DeleteNetnsSymlink()
138: 	}
139: 
140: 	return errors.Join(n.DefaultNode.DeleteNetnsSymlink(), n.netnsNode.DeleteNetnsSymlink())

53: func TestNetnsNodeConfig(t *testing.T) {
54: 	cfg := newSRLTestConfig(t)

56: 	n := newSRLTestNode(t, cfg, nil)
57:

62: 	assert.Equal(t, testNetnsShort, holder.ShortName)
63: 	assert.Equal(t, testNetnsName, holder.LongName)
64: 	assert.Equal(t, n.Cfg.ShortName, holder.GetHostname())
65: 	assert.Equal(t, n.Cfg.Image, holder.Image)
66: 	assert.Equal(t, n.Cfg.RestartPolicy, holder.RestartPolicy)
67: 	assert.Equal(t, n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4Address, holder.MgmtIPv4Address)
68: 	assert.Equal(t, n.Cfg.Sysctls, holder.Sysctls)
69: 	assert.Equal(t, "/bin/sh", holder.Entrypoint)
70: 	assert.Empty(t, holder.Env)
71: 	assert.Empty(t, holder.Binds)
72: 	assert.Equal(t, "true", holder.Labels[clabconstants.InternalNode])
73: 	assert.Equal(t, netnsNodeType, holder.Labels[clabconstants.NodeType])
74: 	assert.Equal(t, n.Cfg.ShortName, holder.Labels[clabconstants.RootNodeName])
75: 	assert.Equal(t, n.Cfg.LongName, holder.Labels[clabconstants.RootNodeLongName])
76: 	assert.Empty(t, n.Cfg.Labels[clabconstants.InternalNode])
77: }

The PR introduces `deployedWithoutNetnsNode` to handle the case where a node was deployed by an older containerlab (before the netns holder feature) and is being started/GetNSPath'd by a new containerlab: the holder container doesn't exist, but the node container does. In that case, fall back to the node's own netns.

Key concerns:

1. `deployedWithoutNetnsNode` is a heuristic: holder NotFound AND node not NotFound. But what if the node container is in `Stopping`/`Paused`/whatever state? Still not NotFound, so falls to node path — fine. What if the holder exists but the node is NotFound (lab partially destroyed)? Then deployedWithoutNetnsNode=false, so `GetNSPath` calls netnsNode.GetNSPath — same as before. Fine.

2. But consider `Start`: with the fallback, the node was deployed without a holder, and Start calls `n.DefaultNode.Start(ctx)`. But wait — the test `TestStartOfNodeDeployedWithoutNetnsNode` mocks GetContainerStatus(node)=Stopped and StartContainer. But note that Start is called with node Stopped and holder NotFound; after Start, the node now runs with its own netns. Subsequent `GetNSPath` works via fallback. Good.

29: // EnsureRunning starts or unpauses the holder, so that the containers of node can join it.
30: func (n *NetnsHolder) EnsureRunning(ctx context.Context, node string) error {
31: 	switch status := n.GetContainerStatus(ctx); status {
32: 	case clabruntime.Running:
33: 	case clabruntime.Created, clabruntime.Stopped:
34: 		if err := n.Start(ctx); err != nil {
35: 			return fmt.Errorf("node %q network namespace container start error: %w", node, err)

52: }

The node's\n// containers join it, so the links and the management address outlive their restarts.\ntype NetnsHolder struct {\n\tDefaultNode\n}\n\nfunc (n *NetnsHolder) Init(cfg *clabtypes.NodeConfig, opts ...NodeOption) error {\n\tn.DefaultNode = *NewDefaultNode(n)\n\tn.Cfg = cfg\n\tn.StopSignal = clabtypes.SIGTERM\n\n\tfor _, o := range opts {\n\t\to(n)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// EnsureRunning starts or unpauses the holder, so that the containers of node can join it.\nfunc (n *NetnsHolder) EnsureRunning(ctx context.Context, node string) error {\n\tswitch status := n.GetContainerStatus(ctx); status {\n\tcase clabruntime.Running:\n\tcase clabruntime.Created, clabruntime.Stopped:\n\t\tif err := n.Start(ctx); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"node %q network namespace container start error: %w\", node, err)\n\t\t}\n\tcase clabruntime.Paused:\n\t\tif err := n.Runtime.UnpauseContainer(ctx, n.Cfg.LongName); err != nil {\n\t\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"node %q network namespace container unpause error: %w\", node, err)\n\t\t}\n\tcase clabruntime.NotFound:\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\n\t\t\t\"node %q network namespace container %q not found; recreate the node\",\n\t\t\tnode, n.Cfg.LongName,\n\t\t)\n\tdefault:\n\t\treturn fmt.Errorf(\"node %q network namespace container %q is %s\",\n\t\t\tnode, n.Cfg.LongName, status)\n\t}\n\n\treturn nil\n}",

16: func (n *sros) newNetnsConfig() *clabtypes.NodeConfig {

83: // GetNSPath retrieves the Namespace Path.
84: func (n *sros) GetNSPath(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
85: 	if n.isStandaloneNode() || (n.isDistributedCardNode() && n.rootCtrName == "") {
86: 		return n.DefaultNode.GetNSPath(ctx)
87: 	} else if n.isDistributedCardNode() {
88: 		return n.Runtime.GetNSPath(ctx, n.rootCtrName)
89: 	}
90: 	return n.netnsNode.GetNSPath(ctx)
91: }

93: // DeleteNetnsSymlink deletes the symlink file created for the container netns.

95: 	var errs []error
96: 
97: 	// if it is the base node, then we need to delete the symlink for all the components.
98: 	if n.isDistributedBaseNode() {
99: 		for _, componentNode := range n.componentNodes {
100: 			errs = append(errs, componentNode.DeleteNetnsSymlink())

106: 	}
107: 
108: 	errs = append(errs, n.DefaultNode.DeleteNetnsSymlink(), n.cleanupParkingNetNS())
109: 
110: 	return errors.Join(errs...)
111: }

If sros nodes deployed pre-holder hit the same issue (Start fails with "recreate the node", GetNSPath fails), the fix is incomplete. Let me check sros.Start and GetNSPath — sros GetNSPath has no deployedWithoutNetnsNode fallback; if netnsNode != nil (which is always true for non-standalone sros?), it would call netnsNode.GetNSPath → error. Let me check sros.go Start.

Also need to check: is `netnsNode` always non-nil for srl when usesNetnsNode()? In initNetnsNode it's only set when usesNetnsNode. So `n.netnsNode == nil` means host-network mode etc.

Important check: in `deployedWithoutNetnsNode`, when netnsNode is nil it would panic — but both callers guard `n.netnsNode == nil ||` before calling it (short-circuit). Only two call sites. OK.

Another check: `n.GetContainerStatus(ctx)` — DefaultNode.GetContainerStatus. Let me verify it exists in default_node.go and what name it uses. Also check runtime status enum values: NotFound, Running, Stopped, Created, Paused.

Edge: what if the node container is NotFound but holder NotFound too (destroyed lab) → Start: netnsNode != nil, deployedWithoutNetnsNode=false → EnsureRunning → error "recreate the node". Good (test covers).

Edge: holder NotFound, node Paused/Created? e.g., node container exists but paused. deployedWithoutNetnsNode = true (status != NotFound) → DefaultNode.Start → StartContainer on paused container? Runtime StartContainer on a paused container errors? Hmm, for docker, starting an already-created container is fine; paused container start → error "cannot start a paused container"? Actually docker: `docker start` on paused container returns an error? I believe it errors ("cannot start a paused container, try unpause"). Edge case, minor.

More important: what about the sros kind having the same gap? That's a real finding candidate: incomplete fix — the same legacy-deployment scenario applies to sros which uses the identical holder mechanism, but sros.Start/GetNSPath lack the fallback. Let me check sros.go Start around 1827.

/source/head/docs/rn/0.83.md:
  Line 43: With Docker and Podman, containerlab captures through packet sockets in the node network namespaces; the command needs root, like `deploy`, but neither the host nor the node needs `tcpdump`. With c9s, the `clabwire` sidecar captures the packets, and long captures are chained without duplicating packets at the handover.

  Line 142: Each `nokia_srlinux` node uses an internal `<node-name>-netns` holder container for its network namespace. /source/head/docs/rn/0.31.md:
  Line 7: As _people of cloud_ [started to use containerlab](../community.md#cilium-bgp-tested-with-containerlab) to test features on the intersection of networking and compute domains, it became evident that containerlab lacked an option to schedule a container in the network namespace of an external container. For example, the need was to start a containerlab lab and stitch it nicely to the k8s kind cluster nodes which run some CNIs that are willing to talk to the network nodes launched in containerlab.


/source/head/docs/cmd/events.md:
  Line 5: The `events` command streams lifecycle updates for every Containerlab resource and augments them with interface change notifications collected from the container network namespaces. The output combines the selected runtime's event feed (for example Docker) with the netlink information that powers `containerlab inspect interfaces`, so you can observe container activity and interface state changes in real time without selecting a specific lab.


/source/head/docs/cmd/capture.md:
  Line 9: - **Docker and Podman**: containerlab opens a packet socket on each interface inside the node's network namespace. Nothing runs in the node, the node image needs no capture tools, and no extra software is needed on the host: the command needs root, like `deploy`. See [How Docker and Podman captures work](#how-docker-and-podman-captures-work).

  Line 90: For each target, containerlab enters the node's network namespace, opens a Linux packet socket (`AF_PACKET`) bound to the interface, and leaves the namespace again; the socket keeps capturing on that interface. This is what `tcpdump` does inside the node, without needing `tcpdump` in the node or on the host. All sockets are opened before the first byte is written, so a capture that cannot start (a node that does not run, a missing interface) fails without output.

  Line 97: The command needs root (to open packet sockets and enter network namespaces), as other lab commands do.

        "text": ")\n\n// BridgeByName returns a *netlink.Bridge referenced by its name.\nfunc BridgeByName(name string) (*netlink.Bridge, error) {\n\tl, err := netlink.LinkByName(name)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"could not lookup %q: %v\", name, err)\n\t}\n\tbr, ok := l.(*netlink.Bridge)\n\tif !ok {\n\t\treturn nil, fmt.Errorf(\"%q already exists but is not a bridge\", name)\n\t}\n\treturn br, nil\n}\n\n// LinkContainerNS creates a symlink for containers network namespace\n// so that it can be managed by iproute2 utility.\nfunc LinkContainerNS(nspath, containerName string) error {\n\tCreateDirectory(\"/run/netns/\", clabconstants.PermissionsDirDefault)\n\tdst := \"/run/netns/\" + containerName\n\tif _, err := os.Lstat(dst); err == nil {\n\t\tos.Remove(dst)\n\t}\n\terr := os.Symlink(nspath, dst)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\treturn err\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// GenMac generates a random MAC address for a given OUI.\nfunc GenMac(oui string) (net.HardwareAddr, error) {\n\tbuf := make([]byte, 3)\n\t_, _ = rand.Read(buf)\n\n\thwa, err := net.ParseMAC(fmt.Sprintf(\"%s:%02x:%02x:%02x\", oui, buf[0], buf[1], buf[2]))\n\treturn hwa, err\n}\n\n// DeleteNetnsSymlink deletes a network namespace and removes the symlink created by LinkContainerNS\n// func.\nfunc DeleteNetnsSymlink(n string) error {\n\tlog.Debug(\"Deleting netns symlink: \", n)\n\tsl := fmt.Sprintf(\"/run/netns/%s\", n)\n\terr := os.Remove(sl)\n\tif err != nil {\n\t\tlog.Debug(\"Failed to delete netns symlink by path:\", sl)\n\t}\n\treturn nil\n}\n\n// ParkingNetnsName returns the deterministic named-netns identifier used to park\n// a container's dataplane interfaces while the container is stopped.\nfunc ParkingNetnsName(containerName string) string {\n\tname := parkingNetnsPrefix + containerName\n\tif len(name) <= maxParkingNetnsNameLen {\n\t\treturn name\n\t}\n\n\tsum := sha1.Sum([]byte(containerName))",

Reasoning
Note: `GetContainerStatus` swallows all inspect errors into `NotFound`. So `deployedWithoutNetnsNode` can also misfire if the Docker daemon is unreachable/temporarily erroring on inspect — then holder status = NotFound (error swallowed) and if the node inspect succeeds (or also fails → NotFound, which makes the second condition false). Actually if both inspects fail, both return NotFound → deployedWithoutNetnsNode = false → normal path → `netnsNode.GetNSPath` → Runtime.GetNSPath → inspect error → returns error. So degraded daemon produces errors, not silent wrong behavior. If only the holder inspect fails (transient) and node is Running → fallback to node's ns path, which for a holder-model deployment is... the node container joined the holder's netns, so node's /proc/<pid>/ns/net is the same netns object. So the path differs but points to the same namespace. Fine.

Now the bigger scenario check: legacy node + `clab deploy` again. Let me look at how deploy handles existing lab: cmd/root or lab.go "isdeployed" checks. Search for "Deployed" state checks in lab.go — e.g., `lab.CheckDeploymentConditions` or skip if deployed. In containerlab, `clab deploy` on an already-deployed lab: nodes' Deploy is called for all nodes; CreateContainer with existing name → docker returns "Conflict. The container name ... is already in use"? Actually I recall containerlab handles that: runtime CreateContainer checks if container exists and removes it? Let me check docker CreateContainer.

30: // DeployResult holds the outcome of a Deploy call.
31: type DeployResult struct {
32: 	Containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer
33: 	// Apply summarizes the reconciliation of an already deployed lab or the dry-run plan;
34: 	// it is nil when Deploy performed a fresh full deployment.
35: 	Apply *ApplyResult
36: 	// RuntimePlan is the remote resource plan produced by a controller-driven runtime dry-run.
37: 	RuntimePlan *clablabruntime.DeployPlan
38: }

40: // Deploy converges the lab to the requested topology. A lab without runtime state is
41: // deployed from scratch, an already deployed lab is reconciled in place.
42: func (c *CLab) Deploy(
43: 	ctx context.Context,
44: 	options *DeployOptions,
45: ) (*DeployResult, error) {
46: 	if options == nil {
47: 		var err error
48: 		options, err = NewDeployOptions(0)
49: 		if err != nil {
50: 			return nil, err
51: 		}
52: 	}
53: 
54: 	if options.reconfigure {
55: 		if options.dryRun {
56: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf(
57: 				"dry-run cannot be combined with reconfigure: " +
58: 					"reconfigure always destroys and redeploys the full lab",
59: 			)
60: 		}
61: 
62: 		containers, err := c.deploy(ctx, options)
63: 		if err != nil {
64: 			return nil, err
65: 		}
66: 
67: 		return &DeployResult{Containers: containers}, nil
68: 	}
69: 
70: 	if c.LabRuntime != nil && options.dryRun {
71: 		planner, ok := c.LabRuntime.(clablabruntime.TopologyPlanner)
72: 		if !ok {
73: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("lab runtime %q does not support dry-run", c.globalRuntimeName)
74: 		}
75: 
76: 		req, err := c.labRuntimeDeployRequest()
77: 		if err != nil {
78: 			return nil, err
79: 		}
80: 		applyLabRuntimeDeployOptions(&req, options)
81: 
82: 		plan, err := planner.Plan(ctx, req)
83: 		if err != nil {
84: 			return nil, err
85: 		}
86: 
87: 		return &DeployResult{RuntimePlan: plan}, nil
88: 	}
89: 
90: 	currentNodes, err := c.runtimeNodeGroups(ctx)
91: 	if err != nil {
92: 		return nil, err
93: 	}
94: 	initialDeploy, err := c.needsInitialDeploy(currentNodes)
95: 	if err != nil {
96: 		return nil, err
97: 	}
98: 	if initialDeploy {
99: 		if options.dryRun {
100: 			return &DeployResult{
101: 				Apply: &ApplyResult{
102: 					DryRun:      true,
103: 					DeployedLab: true,
104: 					LabName:     c.Config.Name,
105: 				},
106: 			}, nil
107: 		}
108: 
109: 		containers, err := c.deploy(ctx, options)
110: 		if err != nil {
111: 			return nil, err
112: 		}
113: 
114: 		return &DeployResult{Containers: containers}, nil
115: 	}
116: 
117: 	if err := c.checkReconcileDeployOptions(options); err != nil {
118: 		return nil, err
119: 	}
120: 
121: 	applyOptions := &ApplyOptions{
122: 		dryRun:             options.dryRun,
123: 		skipPostDeploy:     options.skipPostDeploy,
124: 		skipLabDirFileACLs: options.skipLabDirFileACLs,
125: 		graph:              options.graph,
126: 		finalizeNoop:       true,
127: 		maxWorkers:         options.maxWorkers,
128: 		exportTemplate:     options.exportTemplate,
129: 	}
130: 	applyResult, err := c.apply(ctx, applyOptions, currentNodes)
131: 	if err != nil {
132: 		return nil, err
133: 	}
134: 
135: 	if options.dryRun {
136: 		return &DeployResult{Apply: applyResult}, nil
137: 	}
138: 
139: 	containers, err := c.ListNodesContainers(ctx)
140: 	if err != nil {
141: 		return nil, err
142: 	}
143: 
144: 	return &DeployResult{Containers: containers, Apply: applyResult}, nil
145: }

147: // checkReconcileDeployOptions rejects deploy options that only make sense for a fresh
148: // deployment when deploy is about to reconcile an already deployed lab.
149: func (c *CLab) checkReconcileDeployOptions(options *DeployOptions) error {
150: 	if c.managementNetworkOverridden {
151: 		return fmt.Errorf(
152: 			"management network overrides require a fresh deployment, but lab %q is already "+
153: 				"deployed; use --reconfigure to destroy and redeploy it",
154: 			c.Config.Name,
155: 		)
156: 	}
157: 
158: 	if options.restoreAll != "" || len(options.restoreNodeSnapshots) > 0 {
159: 		return fmt.Errorf(
160: 			"snapshot restore requires a fresh deployment, but lab %q is already deployed; "+
161: 				"use --reconfigure to destroy and redeploy it",
162: 			c.Config.Name,
163: 		)
164: 	}
165: 
166: 	if len(c.nodeFilter) > 0 {
167: 		return fmt.Errorf(
168: 			"node filter is not supported when reconciling deployed lab %q: "+
169: 				"running nodes excluded by the filter would be deleted; "+
170: 				"remove the filter or use --reconfigure",
171: 			c.Config.Name,
172: 		)
173: 	}
174: 
175: 	return nil
176: }

178: // deploy creates a lab that has no managed runtime nodes yet.
179: // skipcq: GO-R1005
180: func (c *CLab) deploy( //nolint: funlen
181: 	ctx context.Context,
182: 	options *DeployOptions,
183: ) ([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, error) {
184: 	if c.LabRuntime != nil {
185: 		return c.deployWithLabRuntime(ctx, options)
186: 	}
187: 
188: 	var err error
189: 
190: 	err = c.ResolveLinks()
191: 	if err != nil {
192: 		return nil, err
193: 	}
194: 
195: 	log.Debugf("lab Conf: %+v", c.Config)
196: 
197: 	if options.reconfigure {
198: 		_ = c.destroy(ctx, uint(len(c.Nodes)), true)
199: 		log.Info("Removing directory", "path", c.TopoPaths.TopologyLabDir())
200: 
201: 		if err := os.RemoveAll(c.TopoPaths.TopologyLabDir()); err != nil {
202: 			return nil, err
203: 		}
204: 	}
205: 
206: 	err = c.prepareLabManagementNetwork(ctx)
207: 	if err != nil {
208: 		return nil, err
209: 	}
210: 
211: 	if err := c.checkTopologyDefinition(ctx); err != nil {
212: 		return nil, err
213: 	}
214: 
215: 	if err := c.prepareDeployArtifacts(ctx, options.skipLabDirFileACLs); err != nil {
216: 		return nil, err
217: 	}
218: 
219: 	// Apply snapshot restore configuration to nodes
220: 	if err := c.configureSnapshotRestore(options); err != nil {
221: 		return nil, err
222: 	}
223: 
224: 	nodesWg, execCollection, nodeFailCh, err := c.createNodes(
225: 		ctx,
226: 		options.maxWorkers,
227: 		options.skipPostDeploy,
228: 	)
229: 	if err != nil {
230: 		return nil, err
231: 	}
232: 
233: 	if err := waitForNodeDeploy(ctx, nodesWg, nodeFailCh); err != nil {
234: 		return nil, err
235: 	}
236: 	if err := c.syncTailscaleProxy(ctx); err != nil {
237: 		return nil, err
238: 	}
239: 	if err := c.SyncMgmtHostRoutes(ctx); err != nil {
240: 		return nil, err
241: 	}
242: 
243: 	// also call deploy on the special nodes endpoints (only host is required for the
244: 	// vxlan stitched endpoints).
245: 	// this must happen after all node workers have finished so that veth pairs created
246: 	// as part of vxlan-stitch links are already deployed before the stitch TC rules are applied.
247: 	eps := c.getSpecialLinkNodes()["host"].GetEndpoints()
248: 	for _, ep := range eps {
249: 		err = ep.Deploy(ctx)
250: 		if err != nil {
251: 			log.Warnf("failed deploying endpoint %s", ep)
252: 		}
253: 	}
254: 
255: 	// Stitch links after node workers and host endpoints have finished.
256: 	// The veth pair is already created by node workers and the VxLAN interface is created
257: 	// by host endpoint deploy; Stitch applies the TC redirect rules to bridge them.
258: 	var linkPostDeployWorkers errgroup.Group
259: 	linkPostDeployWorkers.SetLimit(int(options.maxWorkers))
260: 	for _, link := range c.Links {
261: 		linkPostDeployWorkers.Go(func() error {
262: 			if err := link.PostDeploy(ctx); err != nil {
263: 				log.Warnf("failed post-deploying link: %v", err)
264: 			}
265: 			return nil
266: 		})
267: 	}
268: 	_ = linkPostDeployWorkers.Wait()
269: 
270: 	execCollection.Log()
271: 
272: 	return c.finalize(ctx, options.exportTemplate, options.graph)
273: }
274: 
275: func waitForNodeDeploy(
276: 	ctx context.Context,
277: 	nodesWg *sync.WaitGroup,
278: 	nodeFailCh chan error,
279: ) error {
280: 	if nodesWg != nil {
281: 		nodesWg.Wait()
282: 	}
283: 
284: 	close(nodeFailCh)
285: 
286: 	// Cancellation takes precedence over errors caused by workers unwinding, and
287: 	// prevents post-deploy work from running against a partial lab.
288: 	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
289: 		return err
290: 	}
291: 
292: 	var nodeFailErrs []error
293: 	for nodeErr := range nodeFailCh {
294: 		nodeFailErrs = append(nodeFailErrs, nodeErr)
295: 	}
296: 	if len(nodeFailErrs) > 0 {
297: 		return fmt.Errorf(
298: 			"deployment failed for one or more nodes: %w",
299: 			errors.Join(nodeFailErrs...),
300: 		)
301: 	}
302: 
303: 	return nil
304: }

306: // prepareLabManagementNetwork creates the management networks that are in use
307: // and allocates addresses for the nodes attached to them.
308: func (c *CLab) prepareLabManagementNetwork(
309: 	ctx context.Context,
310: 	existing ...clabtypes.ExistingAddress,
311: ) error {
312: 	if err := c.CreateNetwork(ctx); err != nil {
313: 		return err
314: 	}
315: 
316: 	if err := c.allocateLabManagementIPs(ctx, existing); err != nil {
317: 		return err
318: 	}
319: 
320: 	return c.setMgmtNetLinkBridges()
321: }

323: func (c *CLab) allocateLabManagementIPs(
324: 	ctx context.Context,
325: 	existing []clabtypes.ExistingAddress,
326: ) error {
327: 	preferred := make(map[string]clabtypes.NodeAddresses)
328: 	state, err := c.LoadState()
329: 	if err != nil {
330: 		log.Warn("Ignoring preferred management addresses", "error", err)
331: 	}
332: 
333: 	if state != nil {
334: 		for name, addresses := range state.IPAM {
335: 			preferred[name] = addresses
336: 		}
337: 	}
338: 
339: 	for _, m := range c.allMgmtNetworks() {
340: 		if c.skipMgmtNetwork(m) {
341: 			continue
342: 		}
343: 		nodes := c.mgmtNetNodes(m)
344: 		if m.IPAM.Provider == clabtypes.IPAMProviderRuntime || len(nodes) == 0 {
345: 			continue
346: 		}
347: 
348: 		reserved, err := c.collectReservedManagementAddresses(ctx, m, existing)
349: 		if err != nil {
350: 			return err
351: 		}
352: 
353: 		err = mgmt.AllocateManagementIPs(
354: 			ctx,
355: 			m,
356: 			nodes,
357: 			clabtypes.AllocationOptions{
358: 				Existing:  existing,
359: 				Preferred: preferred,
360: 				Reserved:  reserved,
361: 			},
362: 		)
363: 		if err != nil {
364: 			return err
365: 		}
366: 	}
367: 
368: 	return nil
369: }
370: 
371: func (c *CLab) collectReservedManagementAddresses(
372: 	ctx context.Context,
373: 	m *clabtypes.MgmtNet,
374: 	existing []clabtypes.ExistingAddress,
375: ) ([]netip.Addr, error) {
376: 	var subnets []netip.Prefix
377: 	for _, value := range []string{m.IPv4Subnet, m.IPv6Subnet} {
378: 		if value == "" {
379: 			continue
380: 		}
381: 		subnet, err := netip.ParsePrefix(value)
382: 		if err != nil {
383: 			return nil, fmt.Errorf("management subnet %q: %w", value, err)
384: 		}
385: 		subnets = append(subnets, subnet)
386: 	}
387: 	occupied, err := c.globalRuntime().NetworkAddresses(ctx, subnets)
388: 	if err != nil {
389: 		return nil, err
390: 	}
391: 	type ownerAddress struct {
392: 		containerID string
393: 		address     netip.Addr
394: 	}
395: 	reused := make(map[ownerAddress]bool, len(existing))
396: 	for _, entry := range existing {
397: 		if entry.ContainerID != "" {
398: 			reused[ownerAddress{entry.ContainerID, entry.Address}] = true
399: 		}
400: 	}
401: 
402: 	var reserved []netip.Addr
403: 	for _, entry := range occupied {
404: 		if entry.NetworkName == m.Network &&
405: 			reused[ownerAddress{entry.ContainerID, entry.Address}] {
406: 			continue
407: 		}
408: 		reserved = append(reserved, entry.Address)
409: 	}
410: 	return reserved, nil
411: }

490: func (c *CLab) populateExtraHosts() {
491: 	extraHosts := make([]string, 0, len(c.Nodes))
492: 
493: 	for _, nodeName := range sortedNodeNames(c.Nodes) {
494: 		n := c.Nodes[nodeName]
495: 		if n.Config().MgmtIPv4Address != "" {
496: 			log.Debugf("Adding static ipv4 /etc/hosts entry for %s:%s",
497: 				n.Config().ShortName, n.Config().MgmtIPv4Address)
498: 			extraHosts = append(extraHosts, n.Config().ShortName+":"+n.Config().MgmtIPv4Address)
499: 		}
500: 		if n.Config().MgmtIPv6Address != "" {
501: 			log.Debugf("Adding static ipv6 /etc/hosts entry for %s:%s",
502: 				n.Config().ShortName, n.Config().MgmtIPv6Address)
503: 			extraHosts = append(extraHosts, n.Config().ShortName+":"+n.Config().MgmtIPv6Address)
504: 		}
505: 	}
506: 
507: 	for _, nodeName := range sortedNodeNames(c.Nodes) {
508: 		n := c.Nodes[nodeName]
509: 		if !strings.HasPrefix(n.Config().NetworkMode, "container:") {
510: 			n.Config().ExtraHosts = extraHosts
511: 		}
512: 	}
513: }

515: // certificateAuthoritySetup sets up the certificate authority parameters.
516: func (c *CLab) certificateAuthoritySetup() error {
517: 	// init the Cert storage and CA
518: 	c.Cert.CertStorage = clabcert.NewLocalDirCertStorage(c.TopoPaths)
519: 	c.Cert.CA = clabcert.NewCA()
520: 
521: 	s := c.Config.Settings
522: 
523: 	// Set defaults for the CA parameters
524: 	keySize := 2048
525: 	validityDuration := time.Until(time.Now().AddDate(1, 0, 0)) // 1 year as default
526: 	var extCACert, extCAKey string
527: 
528: 	// check that Settings.CertificateAuthority exists.
529: 	if s != nil && s.CertificateAuthority != nil {
530: 		// if ValidityDuration is set use the value
531: 		if s.CertificateAuthority.ValidityDuration != 0 {
532: 			validityDuration = s.CertificateAuthority.ValidityDuration
533: 		}
534: 
535: 		// if KeyLength is set use the value
536: 		if s.CertificateAuthority.KeySize != 0 {
537: 			keySize = s.CertificateAuthority.KeySize
538: 		}
539: 
540: 		// if external CA cert and key are set, propagate to topopaths
541: 		extCACert = s.CertificateAuthority.Cert
542: 		extCAKey = s.CertificateAuthority.Key
543: 	}
544: 
545: 	// override external ca and key from env vars
546: 	if v := os.Getenv("CLAB_CA_KEY_FILE"); v != "" {
547: 		extCAKey = v
548: 	}
549: 
550: 	if v := os.Getenv("CLAB_CA_CERT_FILE"); v != "" {
551: 		extCACert = v
552: 	}
553: 
554: 	if extCACert != "" && extCAKey != "" {
555: 		err := c.TopoPaths.SetExternalCaFiles(extCACert, extCAKey)
556: 		if err != nil {
557: 			return err
558: 		}
559: 	}
560: 
561: 	// define the attributes used to generate the CA Cert
562: 	caCertInput := &clabcert.CACSRInput{
563: 		CommonName:   c.Config.Name + " lab CA",
564: 		Country:      "US",
565: 		Expiry:       validityDuration,
566: 		Organization: "containerlab",
567: 		KeySize:      keySize,
568: 	}
569: 
570: 	return c.LoadOrGenerateCA(caCertInput)
571: }

573: // createNodes schedules nodes creation and returns a waitgroup for all nodes
574: // with the exec collection created from the exec config of each node.
575: // The exec collection is returned to the caller to ensure that the execution log
576: // is printed after the nodes are created.
577: // Nodes interdependencies are created in this function.
578: func (c *CLab) createNodes(
579: 	ctx context.Context,
580: 	maxWorkers uint,
581: 	skipPostDeploy bool,
582: ) (*sync.WaitGroup, *clabexec.ExecCollection, chan error, error) {
583: 	for _, node := range c.Nodes {
584: 		c.dependencyManager.AddNode(node)
585: 	}
586: 
587: 	// nodes with static mgmt IP should be scheduled before the dynamic ones
588: 	err := c.createStaticDynamicDependency()
589: 	if err != nil {
590: 		return nil, nil, nil, err
591: 	}
592: 
593: 	// create user-defined node dependencies done with `wait-for` property of the deployment stage
594: 	err = c.createWaitForDependency()
595: 	if err != nil {
596: 		return nil, nil, nil, err
597: 	}
598: 
599: 	// make network namespace shared containers start in the right order
600: 	c.createNamespaceSharingDependency()
601: 
602: 	// Add possible additional dependencies here
603: 
604: 	// make sure that there are no unresolvable dependencies, which would deadlock.
605: 	err = c.dependencyManager.CheckAcyclicity()
606: 	if err != nil {
607: 		return nil, nil, nil, err
608: 	}
609: 
610: 	// Buffered so workers never block reporting a failure (at most one failure path per node).
611: 	// With zero nodes, nothing sends on this channel; an empty buffer is fine.
612: 	nodeFailCh := make(chan error, len(c.Nodes))
613: 
614: 	// start scheduling
615: 	NodesWg, execCollection := c.scheduleNodes(ctx, int(maxWorkers), skipPostDeploy, nodeFailCh)
616: 
617: 	return NodesWg, execCollection, nodeFailCh, nil
618: }

629: // deployApplyNodes schedules starts and creates together: a new sidecar can
630: // depend on a stopped target, and a stopped node can depend on a new target.
631: func (c *CLab) deployApplyNodes(ctx context.Context, plan *applyPlan, maxWorkers uint) error {
632: 	nodeNames := sortedStringSet(
633: 		unionStringSets(plan.addedNodeSet, plan.recreatedNodeSet, plan.startNodeSet),
634: 	)
635: 	return c.deployNodes(ctx, nodeNames, maxWorkers, plan.startNodeSet)
636: }

638: func (c *CLab) deployNodes(
639: 	ctx context.Context,
640: 	nodeNames []string,
641: 	maxWorkers uint,
642: 	startNodeSet map[string]struct{},
643: ) error {
644: 	if len(nodeNames) == 0 {
645: 		return nil
646: 	}
647: 
648: 	if maxWorkers == 0 || int(maxWorkers) > len(nodeNames) {
649: 		maxWorkers = uint(len(nodeNames))
650: 	}
651: 	if _, err := c.networkModeNodeOrder(nodeNames); err != nil {
652: 		return err
653: 	}
654: 
655: 	input := make(chan string)
656: 	errCh := make(chan error, len(nodeNames))
657: 	completed := make(map[string]*nodeDeployCompletion, len(nodeNames))
658: 	for _, name := range nodeNames {
659: 		completed[name] = &nodeDeployCompletion{done: make(chan struct{})}
660: 	}
661: 	finish := func(name string, err error) {
662: 		completed[name].err = err
663: 		close(completed[name].done)
664: 		errCh <- err
665: 	}
666: 
667: 	for range maxWorkers {
668: 		go func() {
669: 			for nodeName := range input {
670: 				if _, start := startNodeSet[nodeName]; start {
671: 					log.Info("Starting stopped node", "node", nodeName)
672: 					err := c.Nodes[nodeName].Start(ctx)
673: 					if err != nil {
674: 						err = fmt.Errorf("failed starting node %q: %w", nodeName, err)
675: 					}
676: 					finish(nodeName, err)
677: 					continue
678: 				}
679: 				log.Info("Creating node", "node", nodeName)
680: 				finish(nodeName, c.deployNode(ctx, c.Nodes[nodeName]))
681: 			}
682: 		}()
683: 	}
684: 
685: 	// Wait outside the worker pool. Targets in this operation signal completion
686: 	// directly, avoiding runtime polling and propagating failures to dependents.
687: 	var feedWg sync.WaitGroup
688: 	for _, nodeName := range nodeNames {
689: 		feedWg.Add(1)
690: 		go func(nodeName string) {
691: 			defer feedWg.Done()
692: 			if err := c.waitForNodeDeployTarget(ctx, nodeName, completed); err != nil {
693: 				finish(nodeName, err)
694: 				return
695: 			}
696: 			select {
697: 			case input <- nodeName:
698: 			case <-ctx.Done():
699: 				finish(nodeName, ctx.Err())
700: 			}
701: 		}(nodeName)
702: 	}
703: 	go func() {
704: 		feedWg.Wait()
705: 		close(input)
706: 	}()
707: 
708: 	var errs []error
709: 	for range nodeNames {
710: 		if err := <-errCh; err != nil {
711: 			errs = append(errs, err)
712: 		}
713: 	}
714: 
715: 	if len(errs) > 0 {
716: 		return errors.Join(errs...)
717: 	}
718: 
719: 	return nil
720: }
721: 
722: type nodeDeployCompletion struct {
723: 	done chan struct{}
724: 	// Closing done publishes err to dependent goroutines.
725: 	err error
726: }

728: func (c *CLab) waitForNodeDeployTarget(
729: 	ctx context.Context,
730: 	name string,
731: 	completed map[string]*nodeDeployCompletion,
732: ) error {
733: 	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
734: 		return err
735: 	}
736: 	target := networkModeContainerTarget(c.Nodes[name].Config().NetworkMode)
737: 	if target == "" {
738: 		target = c.Nodes[name].Config().Labels[clabnodestailscale.ParentLabel]
739: 	}
740: 	if completion, selected := completed[target]; selected {
741: 		select {
742: 		case <-completion.done:
743: 			if completion.err != nil {
744: 				return fmt.Errorf(
745: 					"node %q depends on failed node %q: %w",
746: 					name,
747: 					target,
748: 					completion.err,
749: 				)
750: 			}
751: 			return nil
752: 		case <-ctx.Done():
753: 			return ctx.Err()
754: 		}
755: 	}
756: 	return c.waitForApplyNetworkModeTarget(ctx, name)
757: }
758: 
759: // waitForApplyNetworkModeTarget waits until a node's network-mode:
760: // container:<target> target is running, so apply's incremental deploy never
761: // races a newly created or recreated target against its dependent. The
762: // target may be a node in this same apply call (added or recreated
763: // alongside the dependent) or, like fresh deploy, an external container not
764: // managed by this topology.
765: func (c *CLab) waitForApplyNetworkModeTarget(ctx context.Context, nodeName string) error {
766: 	node, exists := c.Nodes[nodeName]
767: 	if !exists {
768: 		return nil
769: 	}
770: 
771: 	target := networkModeContainerTarget(node.Config().NetworkMode)
772: 	if target == "" {
773: 		return nil
774: 	}
775: 
776: 	targetNode, internal := c.Nodes[target]
777: 	if !internal {
778: 		return c.waitForExternalNodeDependencies(ctx, nodeName)
779: 	}
780: 
781: 	runtime := c.globalRuntime()
782: 	if runtime == nil {
783: 		return fmt.Errorf("container runtime is not initialized")
784: 	}
785: 
786: 	return clabruntime.WaitForContainerRunning(ctx, runtime, targetNode.Config().LongName, nodeName)
787: }

792: 		Cert:         c.Cert,
793: 		TopologyName: c.Config.Name,
794: 		TopoPaths:    c.TopoPaths,
795: 		SSHPubKeys:   c.SSHPubKeys,
796: 	}); err != nil {
797: 		return fmt.Errorf("node %q pre-deploy: %w", nodeName, err)
798: 	}
799: 
800: 	if err := node.Deploy(ctx, &clabnodes.DeployParams{Nodes: c.Nodes}); err != nil {
801: 		return fmt.Errorf("node %q deploy: %w", nodeName, err)
802: 	}
803: 
804: 	if err := node.UpdateConfigWithRuntimeInfo(ctx); err != nil {
805: 		log.Errorf("failed to update node runtime information for node %s: %v", nodeName, err)
806: 	}
807: 
808: 	return nil
809: }

816: func (c *CLab) deployLinks(
817: 	ctx context.Context,
818: 	links []clablinks.Link,
819: 	additionalNodeNames []string,
820: ) error {
821: 	touchedNodes := make(map[string]struct{}, len(additionalNodeNames))
822: 	for _, nodeName := range additionalNodeNames {
823: 		touchedNodes[nodeName] = struct{}{}
824: 	}
825: 	for _, link := range links {
826: 		log.Info("Creating link", "link", applyLinkName(link))
827: 
828: 		for _, ep := range clablinks.RuntimeEndpoints(link) {
829: 			if err := ep.Deploy(ctx); err != nil {
830: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed deploying link %s: %w", applyLinkName(link), err)
831: 			}
832: 			touchedNodes[ep.GetNode().GetShortName()] = struct{}{}
833: 		}
834: 
835: 		if err := link.PostDeploy(ctx); err != nil {
836: 			return fmt.Errorf("failed post-deploying link %s: %w", applyLinkName(link), err)
837: 		}
838: 	}
839: 
840: 	for _, nodeName := range sortedStringSet(touchedNodes) {
841: 		node, exists := c.Nodes[nodeName]
842: 		if !exists {
843: 			continue
844: 		}
845: 		if err := node.PostDeployEndpoints(ctx); err != nil {
846: 			return fmt.Errorf("node %q post-deploy links: %w", nodeName, err)
847: 		}
848: 	}
849: 
850: 	return nil
851: }

935: // configureSnapshotRestore configures nodes for snapshot restoration.
936: // It resolves snapshot files for each node and adds the necessary volume mounts
937: // and environment variables to restore from snapshots.
938: func (c *CLab) configureSnapshotRestore(options *DeployOptions) error {
939: 	// Build restore map from per-node specifications
940: 	restoreMap := make(map[string]string)
941: 	for _, mapping := range options.restoreNodeSnapshots {
942: 		parts := strings.SplitN(mapping, "=", 2)
943: 		if len(parts) != 2 {
944: 			return fmt.Errorf("invalid restore format: %s (expected: node=path)", mapping)
945: 		}
946: 		restoreMap[parts[0]] = parts[1]
947: 	}
948: 
949: 	// Track statistics for logging
950: 	var restoredCount, freshCount int
951: 
952: 	// Configure each node
953: 	for _, node := range c.Nodes {
954: 		nodeName := node.Config().ShortName
955: 
956: 		// Resolve snapshot path for this node
957: 		snapshotPath, shouldRestore := resolveNodeSnapshot(nodeName, restoreMap, options.restoreAll)
958: 
959: 		if shouldRestore {
960: 			// Validate snapshot file exists
961: 			if _, err := os.Stat(snapshotPath); os.IsNotExist(err) {
962: 				return fmt.Errorf("snapshot file not found for node %s: %s", nodeName, snapshotPath)
963: 			}
964: 
965: 			// Get absolute path for bind mount
966: 			absPath, err := filepath.Abs(snapshotPath)
967: 			if err != nil {
968: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed to get absolute path for %s: %w", snapshotPath, err)
969: 			}
970: 
971: 			// Add volume mount for snapshot (read-only)
972: 			node.Config().Binds = append(node.Config().Binds,
973: 				fmt.Sprintf("%s:/snapshot.tar:ro", absPath))
974: 
975: 			// Add restore environment variable
976: 			if node.Config().Env == nil {
977: 				node.Config().Env = make(map[string]string)
978: 			}
979: 			node.Config().Env["RESTORE_SNAPSHOT"] = "1"
980: 
981: 			log.Infof("Node %s will restore from: %s", nodeName, snapshotPath)
982: 			restoredCount++
983: 		} else {
984: 			freshCount++
985: 		}
986: 	}
987: 
988: 	// Log deployment mode summary if any restores are configured
989: 	if restoredCount > 0 {
990: 		log.Infof("Deploying %d nodes from snapshots, %d nodes fresh", restoredCount, freshCount)
991: 	}
992: 
993: 	return nil
994: }
995: 
996: // resolveNodeSnapshot determines the snapshot file path for a given node.
997: // Priority: per-node override > restore-all directory > none.
998: func resolveNodeSnapshot(
999: 	nodeName string,
1000: 	restoreMap map[string]string,
1001: 	restoreAll string,
1002: ) (string, bool) {
1003: 	// 1. Check per-node overrides first (highest priority)
1004: 	if snapshotPath, ok := restoreMap[nodeName]; ok {
1005: 		return snapshotPath, true
1006: 	}
1007: 
1008: 	// 2. Check restore-all directory
1009: 	if restoreAll != "" {
1010: 		// Look for {nodename}.tar in directory
1011: 		snapshotPath := filepath.Join(restoreAll, nodeName+".tar")
1012: 		if _, err := os.Stat(snapshotPath); err == nil {
1013: 			return snapshotPath, true
1014: 		}
1015: 
1016: 		// Not found - this is OK, just deploy normally
1017: 		log.Debugf("No snapshot found for node %s in %s, deploying normally", nodeName, restoreAll)
1018: 		return "", false
1019: 	}
1020: 
1021: 	// 3. No restore specified
1022: 	return "", false
1023: }

*CLab) deployNodes(\n639: \tctx context.Context,\n640: \tnodeNames []string,\n641: \tmaxWorkers uint,\n642: \tstartNodeSet map[string]struct{},\n643: ) error {\n644: \tif len(nodeNames) == 0 {\n645: \t\t}()\n683: \t}\n684: \n685: \t// Wait outside the worker pool. The apply plan compares the current topology state vs desired. For the srl node, the desired config now includes the holder. Would apply detect the node as "needs recreation" (since its runtime config differs — network-mode changed from bridge to container:holder)? If apply detects a diff, it would recreate the node — destroying the running legacy node's config (unless preserved). The comment in the PR says "keeps working ... until it is recreated" — implying reconcile may or may not recreate it. Let me check `apply` logic: `c.runtimeNodeGroups`, `needsInitialDeploy`, apply plan building — `plan.recreatedNodeSet` etc. Look at apply.go to see how it computes diffs (ComputeDiff on NodeConfig). The legacy node's stored config (in lab dir state) has NetworkMode="" and mgmt network attached; the new desired config would have... wait, actually for the *node* config, `n.Cfg` still has NetworkMode="" (containerConfig is only used at CreateContainer time). The stored/running config from old clab would be similar. Does ComputeDiff consider the holder? The node's config is unchanged. So apply would consider the node unchanged, not recreate it — it would just "start" it if stopped. That matches the PR: Start handles legacy.

But wait — there's a subtlety: after apply, if the legacy node is started via the new Start path (DefaultNode.Start), the holder container was never created. Then `GetNSPath` fallback handles ns path. But links: during apply, links to the legacy node — endpoints attach to the node's netns. Endpoints use the node's ns path (via GetNSPath fallback) — should work.

However: does apply recreate the node when it detects the holder missing? Let me check apply.go for how it determines recreation, and whether it consults the netns holder existence. If apply only diffs topology config, the legacy node stays. Good — that's the intent.

But here's a potential real bug: after the legacy node is started via `DefaultNode.Start`, `n.GetNSPath` falls back to the node's own ns path — good. But what about `Stop`? Stop stops the node (DefaultNode.Stop) and holder is NotFound → returns nil. Then Start again → legacy path again. OK.

And `Delete` — deletes both; holder DeleteContainer on NotFound container — check DefaultNode.Delete: does it handle NotFound gracefully? Let me check DefaultNode.Delete.

Now let me consider the **`Start` fallback and the netns symlink**: For the legacy node path, `Start` returns `n.DefaultNode.Start(ctx)` without calling `linkNetns`. For a legacy node, does the netns symlink exist? It was created by the old clab version at deploy time (`/run/netns/<LongName>` pointing to the node's then-current /proc/<pid>/ns/net). If the node container was restarted by docker restart policy (pid changed), the symlink is stale. The new `Start` doesn't refresh it. But `GetNSPath` (used by netem tools etc.) doesn't use the symlink — it uses Runtime.GetNSPath with live PID, or falls back to the /run/netns link. Hmm: `Runtime.GetNSPath` for a *stopped* container falls back to `/run/netns/<cID>` — note `cID` here is the container name passed (`d.OverwriteNode.GetContainerName()`). For the legacy node started fresh, PID > 0 → live path. Good.

But wait — is the missing `linkNetns` in the legacy Start path a real issue? Compare: the holder path calls `linkNetns` after start to keep the symlink fresh. The legacy path doesn't refresh the symlink. For legacy nodes, the symlink was created by the old clab at deploy and could be stale after restart. Consumers: `ip netns` commands users run manually, and `GetNSPath`'s own fallback for stopped containers. Since the PR explicitly says legacy nodes "keep working until they are recreated", refreshing the symlink would be more correct but it's a minor gap: after restarting a legacy node, `docker exec` tools like netem use `GetNSPath` (live), so unaffected. External `ip netns exec` usage by users could hit a stale symlink. Is this worth flagging? It's P4-ish, speculative-ish. Hmm, but actually — wait. Does the legacy node even have the symlink? Old clab versions: the netns symlink feature (LinkContainerNS) predates the holder (it's been there for years). Yes, old clab created it for srl nodes. After a host reboot with `restart: unless-stopped` policy... actually for legacy nodes, what restart policy did old clab set? The holder feature sets unless-stopped default. Legacy srl nodes had no restart policy default ("no"?). Containerlab has long set restart policy... I don't remember. This is getting speculative; I'll skip or put in coverage notes.

Now the more significant consistency issue: **`sros` kind shares the same holder mechanism but wasn't fixed.** sros.Start (line 1827) calls `EnsureRunning` for non-standalone nodes; if a legacy srsim lab (deployed before holder feature) is started with new clab → error "not found; recreate the node". And sros.GetNSPath (netns.go:90) returns `n.netnsNode.GetNSPath` → error. Same legacy-deployment problem. The PR fixes only srl. Is sros affected? The sros holder feature (srsim-netns) came in 0.80 per release notes: "SR-SIM distributed chassis components are attached to an internal namespace pause container". So legacy srsim labs deployed on 0.79 hit the same issue. This is a real inconsistency finding — the PR's root-cause fix is placed in the srl node only, while the shared mechanism (`NetnsHolder.EnsureRunning`, `GetNSPath`) has another consumer. Per the ponytail rule ("fix the shared function once — one guard there"), a shared guard would cover both. But the guard depends on node-specific semantics (sros has componentNodes, standalone/distributed logic), so a shared fix is more complex. Still, flagging the sros gap is legitimate: P2/P3. Let me verify sros behavior more: does sros have a `deployedWithoutNetns` equivalent? grep showed no. And sros_test has "TestStartRequiresNetnsNode"-like test at line 884 expecting error. Let me check sros GetNSPath fallback for distributed card nodes uses rootCtrName. For a legacy srsim lab: netnsNode != nil, rootCtrName probably empty for base node → `n.netnsNode.GetNSPath(ctx)` → DefaultNode.GetNSPath → Runtime.GetNSPath(ctx, "clab-x-netns") → container not found → error "namespace path not available". So legacy srsim labs break on tools (netem, capture, wireshark) and on Start.

Hmm, but wait — is `n.netnsNode` non-nil for sros by default? Check sros init: `initNetnsNode` equivalent. Let me check quickly.

Reasoning
Confirmed: sros has the same holder mechanism for distributed (srsim) base nodes, with no legacy fallback. So the PR fixes the legacy gap only for `srl`. This is a legit finding — same trigger: a lab deployed by an older containerlab (before the holder) is managed by the new binary. For srsim base nodes, `Start` errors with "recreate the node" and `GetNSPath` fails. Severity: same class as the bug being fixed (P2). It's a completeness gap rather than a regression introduced by this PR; the PR introduces the fix semantics, and sros lacks it. I'd rate P3 maybe — since the PR didn't worsen sros. But per review rules "Focus on issues introduced or materially worsened by this PR". The PR establishes a fix pattern and explicitly addresses "nodes deployed by a containerlab before the holder" — leaving the sibling kind broken is the classic Ponytail "patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken" rule, which the supplied ponytail.mdc explicitly states as a criterion. So flagging it is aligned. I'll rate P2 (correctness/reliability defect for the same user scenario the PR claims to fix).

Now check the sros `Stop` at 1844: `if n.GetContainerStatus(ctx) == clabruntime.Stopped return nil` — for legacy srsim, node Running → ParkEndpoints etc. Then Start fails. OK.

Next, examine the fallback more carefully for a subtle correctness trap in `deployedWithoutNetnsNode`: The condition `holder NotFound && node not NotFound`. Consider a fresh deployment in progress: Deploy creates holder (Running), then node created/started. Fine.

Consider **`clab start` on a lab whose holder container was removed manually** (e.g., user did `docker rm clab-x-srl1-netns` while node stopped). New behavior: Start → legacy path → DefaultNode.Start starts the node container. But the node container was created with `NetworkMode: container:clab-x-srl1-netns`! Starting a container whose netns-donor container was removed: docker refuses to start? When the donor container is removed, docker... Actually docker keeps the netns alive as long as the joined container exists; removing the donor container — I believe docker errors on removing it while others join? No, docker allows removing the donor; the joined containers keep working (netns persists). On restart of the joined container, docker start fails with "cannot join network namespace of a non running container"? Something like that. So in that case Start would fail at StartContainer with a docker error — before this PR, it failed earlier with the clearer "recreate the node" error. Now the error message becomes an obscure docker error instead of the actionable one. Minor UX regression: P3/P4. Hmm, actually is that true? When donor is removed, starting the joined container: Docker returns 404 for the netns container? The error is "cannot join network of a non running container" or similar. Either way the start fails; the message quality degrades. But wait — does the fallback even trigger here? holder NotFound (removed), node Stopped → yes, deployedWithoutNetnsNode true → DefaultNode.Start → StartContainer fails with docker error about network mode. Before: EnsureRunning → NotFound → "recreate the node" clear message. This is a real behavioral regression in error clarity for that scenario. But how likely is a user to `docker rm` the internal holder? The holder is hidden from inspect unless --all, and removed with the node. Could also happen if holder crashed and auto-removed? AutoRemove is not set for the holder (AutoRemove not set in newNetnsConfig — DefaultNode AutoRemove false). Restart policy unless-stopped means the holder restarts, not removed. So the trigger is manual removal of an internal container. P3 at most; arguably acceptable tradeoff. I might mention it as P4.

Hmm, but wait — actually there's a subtler issue: what if the node container was created by the *new* clab with `container:holder` mode, the holder is NotFound (deleted), node Stopped → Start now attempts `StartContainer` on the node which will fail with a confusing error rather than "recreate the node". The test `TestStartOfNodeDeployedWithoutNetnsNode` only mocks StartContainer success; there's no test for the "holder deleted, new-model node stopped" case. This is exactly the ambiguity of the status-based heuristic: it cannot distinguish "legacy node with own netns" from "holder-model node whose holder was deleted". Impact: misleading error. P3.

Next: **GetNSPath dual-inspect cost**: each GetNSPath call now does 2 container inspects (holder + node) in the fallback path only... no wait — `deployedWithoutNetnsNode` is evaluated on EVERY GetNSPath call, even in the normal path: it calls `n.netnsNode.GetContainerStatus(ctx)` (1 inspect) and, only if NotFound, `n.GetContainerStatus` (another). In the normal path (holder Running), it's 1 inspect per GetNSPath call, then netnsNode.GetNSPath does its own inspect (GetContainerStatus inside? no — `netnsNode.GetNSPath` → DefaultNode.GetNSPath → Runtime.GetNSPath → 1 inspect). So normal path: 2 inspects instead of 1. Fallback: 3. GetNSPath is called per endpoint per deploy/link-op, and by tools like netem (per node). Inspect is cheap (~ms). This is a modest, acceptable cost — not a real finding, maybe worth a note. Actually, the code evaluates `n.netnsNode == nil || n.deployedWithoutNetnsNode(ctx)` — when netnsNode != nil and holder Running, deployedWithoutNetnsNode does one extra inspect per call. With many links (srl nodes can have dozens of endpoints) during deploy, each endpoint deploy calls GetNSPath → +1 inspect each. Docker inspect is a fast HTTP call; hundreds of calls add maybe a second total. Fine, not worth flagging beyond a P4 note. Actually, hmm — where is GetNSPath called during deploy? OK. Now, another thing to verify: in `TestStartOfNodeDeployedWithoutNetnsNode`, the node status is `Stopped`, and `DefaultNode.Start` calls `StartContainer` then `RestoreEndpoints`. RestoreEndpoints for a legacy node — does it park/restore? The mock runtime only expects StartContainer. RestoreEndpoints presumably checks whether there are parked endpoints (persisted state) and no-ops if none. And `RunExecFromConfig` — for srl, exec commands? That's on DefaultNode — `d.RunExecFromConfig` reads config exec commands... For the srl node with no exec config, no-op. The test passes presumably (mock runtime strict: gomock would fail on unexpected calls). So RestoreEndpoints and RunExecFromConfig make no runtime calls in this test config. OK.

Now, one more important check: `n.Start` in the new code — when legacy (deployedWithoutNetnsNode), it returns `n.DefaultNode.Start(ctx)`. But `DefaultNode.Start` errors if node is NotFound. In the fallback condition, node is NOT NotFound (could be Running/Stopped/Created/Paused/Restarting/Removing). If node is Running → skip. If Created → StartContainer works. If Paused → docker start on paused → error? Docker: "cannot start a paused container, try unpause"? Actually I think `docker start` on a paused container errors. Edge: legacy node paused → Start fails with docker error. Before: failed with "recreate the node". Similar error quality. Minor.

Now — a potentially more serious issue: **`Stop` for the legacy node parks endpoints**. `DefaultNode.Stop` → `ParkEndpoints` → creates a parking netns and moves interfaces. Then `Start` → RestoreEndpoints restores them. That works for legacy nodes too since it's node-agnostic. Fine.

Next, check the state machine interplay: `deployedWithoutNetnsNode` returns true also when holder NotFound and node Restarting. Then Start → DefaultNode.Start → status Restarting → falls through switch → StartContainer → docker error "container is restarting"? Edge again.

Now let me examine the third changed file diff part: srl.go Start change only. And tests. Coverage seems reasonable: three new tests.

Now let me check `GetNSPath` fallback path for a legacy node where `n.Cfg.IsRootNamespaceBased` — `usesNetnsNode()` is false when IsRootNamespaceBased, so netnsNode == nil → first branch. Fine.

One more: `deployedWithoutNetnsNode` doc comment is a bit garbled: "as a node deployed by a containerlab before the holder does until it is recreated" — grammar issue. Minor (P4 readability?). Probably not worth a finding on its own; could fold into another finding. It's genuinely confusing: "before the holder does until it is recreated". I could flag as P4 clarity. Given review quality bar, small but legit.

Now the biggest remaining question: does `apply` (reconcile) interplay break for legacy nodes? E.g., `clab deploy` on legacy lab: apply computes plan; for the srl node, does it detect the *missing holder*? Let me check apply.go's plan logic — specifically whether it inspects node container existence (the legacy node exists, so it's in `runningNodeSet`). Then PostDeploy etc. During apply, links: `deployLinks` → ep.Deploy → for existing endpoints unchanged, skipped. Should be fine.

But actually — wait. There's something important in apply: does apply recreate nodes whose *holder* is missing? Let me check the apply plan code to see how it decides recreation — maybe it uses `GetContainers` which handles holder-missing. Let me look at apply.go briefly for "recreate".

787: func (c *CLab) planNodeReconciliation(ctx context.Context, plan *applyPlan) error {
788: 	if plan == nil || plan.currentNodes == nil {
789: 		return nil
790: 	}
791: 
792: 	var oldTopo *clabtypes.Topology
793: 	if plan.state != nil {
794: 		oldTopo = plan.state.Topology
795: 	}
796: 
797: 	for nodeName := range plan.currentNodes {
798: 		node, exists := c.Nodes[nodeName]
799: 		if !exists {
800: 			continue
801: 		}
802: 		if _, added := plan.addedNodeSet[nodeName]; added {
803: 			continue
804: 		}
805: 
806: 		oldNodeConfig := c.resolveNodeConfigFromTopology(oldTopo, nodeName)
807: 		newNodeConfig := c.resolveNodeConfigFromTopology(c.Config.Topology, nodeName)
808: 		diff := node.ComputeDiff(oldNodeConfig, newNodeConfig)
809: 		plan.nodeDiffs[nodeName] = diff
810: 
811: 		result, err := node.GetReconcilePlan(ctx, diff)
812: 		if err != nil {
813: 			return fmt.Errorf("reconcile planning failed for node %q: %w", nodeName, err)
814: 		}
815: 		if plan.isNonContainerNode(nodeName) && result.Action != clabtypes.TopologyDiffActionNone {
816: 			return fmt.Errorf(
817: 				"node %q is externally managed and cannot be %s for %s",
818: 				nodeName,
819: 				result.Action,
820: 				configDriftReason(diff),
821: 			)
822: 		}
823: 
824: 		switch result.Action {
825: 		case clabtypes.TopologyDiffActionRestart:
826: 			plan.restartNodeSet[nodeName] = struct{}{}
827: 			plan.nodeChangeReasons[nodeName] = configDriftReason(diff)
828: 		case clabtypes.TopologyDiffActionRecreate:
829: 			plan.recreatedNodeSet[nodeName] = struct{}{}
830: 			plan.nodeChangeReasons[nodeName] = configDriftReason(diff)
831: 		}
832: 	}
833: 
834: 	return nil
835: }

837: func configDriftReason(diff *clabtypes.TopologyDiff) string {
838: 	if diff == nil || len(diff.Fields) == 0 {
839: 		return "config drift"
840: 	}
841: 
842: 	return "config drift: " + strings.Join(diff.Fields, ", ")
843: }

845: func (c *CLab) reconcileNodes(ctx context.Context, plan *applyPlan) error {
846: 	if plan == nil || plan.currentNodes == nil {
847: 		return nil
848: 	}
849: 
850: 	for nodeName := range plan.currentNodes {
851: 		node, exists := c.Nodes[nodeName]
852: 		if !exists {
853: 			continue
854: 		}
855: 		if _, added := plan.addedNodeSet[nodeName]; added {
856: 			continue
857: 		}
858: 		if plan.isRootNamespaceNode(nodeName) {
859: 			continue
860: 		}
861: 		// Recreated nodes are handled exclusively by the apply pipeline
862: 		// (park -> delete -> deploy -> restore). Calling Reconcile here would
863: 		// delete the container before parkRecreatedNodes can capture its
864: 		// interfaces, breaking the recreate flow.
865: 		if _, recreated := plan.recreatedNodeSet[nodeName]; recreated {
866: 			continue
867: 		}
868: 
869: 		diff := plan.nodeDiffs[nodeName]
870: 
871: 		result, err := node.Reconcile(ctx, diff)
872: 		if err != nil {
873: 			return fmt.Errorf("reconcile failed for node %q: %w", nodeName, err)
874: 		}
875: 
876: 		if result.Action == clabtypes.TopologyDiffActionRestart {
877: 			if err := c.waitNodeRunning(ctx, node); err != nil {
878: 				return err
879: 			}
880: 			if err := c.waitNodeHealthyIfAvailable(ctx, node); err != nil {
881: 				return err
882: 			}
883: 		}
884: 	}
885: 
886: 	return nil
887: }

889: func (p *applyPlan) linkNeedsDeploy(link clablinks.Link) bool {
890: 	for _, ep := range clablinks.RuntimeEndpoints(link) {
891: 		key := endpointKeyFromEndpoint(ep)
892: 		if _, parked := p.parkedNodeSet[key.node]; !parked {
893: 			if _, added := p.addedNodeSet[key.node]; added {
894: 				return true
895: 			}
896: 		}
897: 		if _, live := p.liveEndpointSet[key]; !live {
898: 			return true
899: 		}
900: 	}
901: 
902: 	return !p.linkIntact(link)
903: }
904: 
905: func (p *applyPlan) linkIntact(link clablinks.Link) bool {
906: 	endpoints := clablinks.RuntimeEndpoints(link)
907: 	if len(endpoints) != 2 || len(p.liveEndpointInfo) == 0 {
908: 		return true
909: 	}
910: 
911: 	left, leftOK := p.liveEndpointInfo[endpointKeyFromEndpoint(endpoints[0])]
912: 	right, rightOK := p.liveEndpointInfo[endpointKeyFromEndpoint(endpoints[1])]
913: 	if !leftOK || !rightOK {
914: 		return false
915: 	}
916: 
917: 	if bridgeMasterMismatch(endpoints[0], left) || bridgeMasterMismatch(endpoints[1], right) {
918: 		return false
919: 	}
920: 
921: 	return left.PeerIndex != 0 &&
922: 		right.PeerIndex != 0 &&
923: 		left.PeerIndex == right.Index &&
924: 		right.PeerIndex == left.Index
925: }
926: 
927: // bridgeMasterMismatch reports whether the live interface of a bridge endpoint is
928: // attached to a bridge other than the one the endpoint resolves to, e.g. after a
929: // mgmt-net link moved to another management network. mgmt-net endpoints whose
930: // management network bridge is not resolved are not checked.
931: func bridgeMasterMismatch(ep clablinks.Endpoint, live clablinks.OwnedInterface) bool {
932: 	node := ep.GetNode()
933: 	if node.GetLinkEndpointType() != clablinks.LinkEndpointTypeBridge ||
934: 		clablinks.IsUnresolvedMgmtBridgeEndpoint(ep) {
935: 		return false
936: 	}
937: 
938: 	return live.MasterName != node.GetShortName()
939: }

943: 		return nil
944: 	}

950: 	}

952: 		if _, added := p.addedNodeSet[nodeName]; !added {
953: 			nodeNames = append(nodeNames, nodeName)
954: 		}
955: 	}
956: 
957: 	sort.Strings(nodeNames)
958: 	return nodeNames
959: }
