- Exact code added in `nodes/srl/netns.go`:
  - New import `clabruntime "github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/runtime"`.
  - `func (n *srl) deployedWithoutNetnsNode(ctx) bool` → `n.netnsNode.GetContainerStatus(ctx) == clabruntime.NotFound && n.GetContainerStatus(ctx) != clabruntime.NotFound`.
  - `GetNSPath` guard changed from `if n.netnsNode == nil` to `if n.netnsNode == nil || n.deployedWithoutNetnsNode(ctx)`.
  - `nodes/srl/srl.go` `Start` (line ~421) guard changed to `if n.netnsNode == nil || n.deployedWithoutNetnsNode(ctx) { return n.DefaultNode.Start(ctx) }`.
- New tests in `nodes/srl/netns_test.go` (lines ~217–268): `TestGetNSPathOfNodeDeployedWithoutNetnsNode`, updated `TestStartRequiresNetnsNode` (mocks with AnyTimes), asserts "recreate the node" error still occurs when both holder and node are NotFound.
- Key verified facts:
  - `NetnsHolder.EnsureRunning` (`nodes/netns_holder.go:30`) errors with "node %q network namespace container %q not found; recreate the node" on `NotFound` — base behavior that broke legacy deployments.
  - `DefaultNode.GetContainerStatus` (`nodes/default_node.go:1160`) → `d.Runtime.GetContainerStatus(ctx, d.OverwriteNode.GetContainerName())`; `srl` does not override it.
  - Docker runtime `GetContainerStatus` (`runtime/docker/docker.go:1942`) swallows all inspect errors into `NotFound`.
  - Docker runtime `GetNSPath` (`runtime/docker/docker.go:1084`): running container → `/proc/<pid>/ns/net`; stopped → `/run/netns/<name>` fallback.
  - `sros` kind shares the same netns holder mechanism but has NO equivalent fallback: `sros.Start` (`nodes/sros/sros.go:1827`) calls `EnsureRunning` unconditionally for non-standalone nodes; `sros.GetNSPath` (`nodes/sros/netns.go:84-90`) has no `deployedWithoutNetnsNode` check — candidate finding (incomplete/one-sided fix).
  - `utils.LinkContainerNS` (`utils/netlink.go:57`) creates `/run/netns/<name>` symlink; legacy Start path does NOT call `linkNetns` (potential stale symlink for legacy nodes — minor/speculative).
  - `core/deploy.go` Deploy reconciles already-deployed labs in place (apply flow); legacy node config diff likely empty → not recreated, matching PR comment "until it is recreated".
  - No docs/release-note changes in the PR; `docs/rn/0.83.md` mentions the holder feature; `.cursor/rules/release-note-review.mdc` requires checking `docs/rn/` changes (none present — assess whether a release note entry is warranted for this user-visible fix).

- Edge cases analyzed: holder NotFound + node Paused/Created → falls to `DefaultNode.Start` (may error on paused container); transient holder inspect failure with node Running → falls back to node's own ns path which shares the same netns (harmless); daemon fully down → errors surface as before.

56: 		MgmtIPv4Address:       n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4Address,
57: 		MgmtIPv4AddressAuto:   n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4AddressAuto,
58: 		MgmtIPv4PrefixLength:  n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4PrefixLength,
59: 		MgmtIPv6Address:       n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6Address,
60: 		MgmtIPv6AddressAuto:   n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6AddressAuto,
61: 		MgmtIPv6PrefixLength:  n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6PrefixLength,
62: 		MgmtIPv4Gateway:       n.Cfg.MgmtIPv4Gateway,
63: 		MgmtIPv6Gateway:       n.Cfg.MgmtIPv6Gateway,
64: 		MacAddress:            n.Cfg.MacAddress,
65: 		Aliases:               n.Cfg.Aliases,
66: 		DNS:                   n.Cfg.DNS,
67: 		ExtraHosts:            n.Cfg.ExtraHosts,
68: 		Labels:                labels,
69: 		Runtime:               n.Cfg.Runtime,
70: 		ResultingPortBindings: n.Cfg.ResultingPortBindings,
71: 	}
72: }
73: 
74: func (n *sros) cleanupParkingNetNS() error {
75: 	name := clabutils.ParkingNetnsName(n.Cfg.LongName)
76: 	if _, err := clabutils.GetNamedNetNS(name); err != nil {
77: 		return nil
78: 	}
79: 
80: 	return netns.DeleteNamed(name)
81: }
82: 
83: // GetNSPath retrieves the Namespace Path.
84: func (n *sros) GetNSPath(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
85: 	if n.isStandaloneNode() || (n.isDistributedCardNode() && n.rootCtrName == "") {
86: 		return n.DefaultNode.GetNSPath(ctx)
87: 	} else if n.isDistributedCardNode() {
88: 		return n.Runtime.GetNSPath(ctx, n.rootCtrName)
89: 	}
90: 	return n.netnsNode.GetNSPath(ctx)
91: }
92: 
93: // DeleteNetnsSymlink deletes the symlink file created for the container netns.
94: func (n *sros) DeleteNetnsSymlink() error {
95: 	var errs []error
96: 
97: 	// if it is the base node, then we need to delete the symlink for all the components.
98: 	if n.isDistributedBaseNode() {
99: 		for _, componentNode := range n.componentNodes {
100: 			errs = append(errs, componentNode.DeleteNetnsSymlink())
101: 		}
102: 		if n.netnsNode != nil {
103: 			errs = append(errs, n.netnsNode.DeleteNetnsSymlink())
104: 		}
105: 		errs = append(errs, clabutils.DeleteNetnsSymlink(n.Cfg.LongName))
106: 	}
107: 
108: 	errs = append(errs, n.DefaultNode.DeleteNetnsSymlink(), n.cleanupParkingNetNS())
109: 
110: 	return errors.Join(errs...)
111: }

Reasoning
Confirmed the sros parity gap: for a distributed base node (`n.netnsNode != nil`, not standalone/card), `sros.Start` calls `n.netnsNode.EnsureRunning(ctx, ...)` unconditionally, and `sros.GetNSPath` returns `n.netnsNode.GetNSPath(ctx)` — no legacy fallback. A legacy srsim deployment (created before the netns holder feature) hit by the new binary: `Start` → EnsureRunning → NotFound → "recreate the node" error; `GetNSPath` → holder inspect fails → error. So `clab start`/`stop`-then-`start` and link operations (netem, ExecFunction) fail on legacy sros distributed nodes.

Now, is this actually reachable? For a legacy sros distributed node: node container exists with its own netns (old model: base node has its own netns; components joined it? In the pre-holder model, srsim distributed base had components with NetworkMode container:<base>? Let me think — before the holder, did srsim distributed nodes even exist? The srsim distributed (line card) support is quite recent (added around the same time as the holder?). If the holder feature and srsim distributed support were added in the same release, then no legacy distributed deployments exist without the holder, making the parity gap theoretical. Let me check the release notes: `docs/rn/0.83.md` mentioned the holder feature. Let me check when srsim distributed was added — check docs/rn for srsim.

So legacy distributed sros nodes deployed in 0.79 or earlier DO exist without a holder — wait, but in 0.79 srsim distributed existed without the holder? 240: 
241: ```bash
242: containerlab tools netem set -n r1 -t netem.clab.yml -i eth1 --delay 5ms
243: containerlab tools netem show -t netem.clab.yml
244: ```
245: 
246: Thanks @kaelemc #3409
247: 
248: ## SR-SIM netns ownership
249: 
250: SR-SIM distributed chassis components are attached to an internal namespace pause container — the same way Kubernetes holds pod namespaces — so any component container can be killed and brought back without losing the network namespace. The internal container is hidden from `inspect` output unless `--all` is set.
251: 
252: Thanks @kaelemc #3397
253: 
254: ## Fortinet FortiProxy
255: 
256: The new `fortinet_fortiproxy` kind aliases the [`fortinet_fortigate`](../manual/kinds/fortinet_fortigate.md) kind. For both kinds, the node's `license` file is now mounted into the vrnetlab container, where a TFTP server serves it to the VM for license activation.
257: 
258: Thanks @KarelChanivecky #3228
259: 
260: ## `network-mode: container:` with apply
261: 
262: `apply` no longer rejects nodes with `network-mode: container:<target>`, so sidecars sharing another node's netns can be added or changed on a running lab. When the target node is recreated, dependent nodes are recreated as well, and they wait for their target independently of the `--max-workers` pool.
263: 
264: Thanks @steiler #3383
265: 
266: ## Miscellaneous
267: 
268: - SR Linux interface names are validated when a lab is deployed: only the `ethernet-L/P`, `ethernet-L/P/C`, or short `eL-P`, `eL-P-C` forms are accepted. A post-deploy panic for restored, runtime-discovered endpoints without topology links is fixed too. [#3395](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3395)
269: - Bridges added to a running lab are now treated as new nodes on `apply`. [#3438](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3438)
270: - Interface names passed to `vxlan-stitch` links are sanitized, which fixes SR-SIM deployments with long node or interface names. [#3437](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3437)
271: - `inspect --all` merges repeated cells again when `--wide`/`-w` is set. [#3378](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3378)
272: - Canonical image names are resolved correctly for registries addressed as `host:port`, fixing image pulls and auth lookups for such registries. [#3391](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3391)
273: - External management access works again for setuid-root installs on iptables-legacy backends, where `iptables` refused to run with differing real and effective UIDs. [#3353](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3353)
274: - Fixed a missing client context in the Podman runtime when copying configuration to containers. [#3364](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3364)
275: - Bind mounts in the Podman runtime carry the `:z` option so files are accessible across security contexts. [#3347](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3347)
276: - `sonic-vs` marks its wire interfaces (`ethN`) ARP-off and IPv6-off so only the port interface answers, preventing stale ARP entries with the wrong MAC. [#3390](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3390)
277: - `vr-ftosv` link endpoints accept the `ethernet1/1/X`, `ethernet 1/1/X`, and `1/1/X` names in addition to `ethX`. [#3354](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3354)
278: - The quick setup script installs Docker 29.8.1 on Ubuntu 26.04, uses the official Docker repository for CentOS, checks for an SSH daemon, and relies on the RPM repo config file instead of dnf/yum commands. [#3424](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3424) [#3400](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3400) [#3431](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3431)
279: - Fixed a flaky management interface update when Cisco IOL nodes are redeployed. [#3392](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3392)

(Showing lines 240-279 of 280. Use offset=280 to continue.)
</content>

Reasoning
Confirmed. Now, another subtle point on the fallback heuristic. `deployedWithoutNetnsNode` = holder NotFound AND node not NotFound. But `NetnsHolder.GetContainerStatus` — NetnsHolder embeds DefaultNode; `GetContainerStatus` uses `d.OverwriteNode.GetContainerStatus(ctx)` where holder's OverwriteNode is itself → `d.Runtime.GetContainerStatus(ctx, holder.LongName)`. OK.

Now consider **the srl node whose holder is NotFound but the node itself is NotFound** — e.g., after `clab destroy` partially failed or a fresh lab (netnsNode initialized, no containers yet). Then `deployedWithoutNetnsNode` false → `EnsureRunning` → NotFound → "recreate the node" error. Correct behavior for fresh labs (the EnsureRunning path expects Deploy to create it).

But here's a real edge: **daemon restart / docker down** — when the Docker daemon is down, `GetContainerStatus` for the holder returns NotFound (inspect error swallowed, docker.go:1946-1948). And `n.GetContainerStatus(ctx)` for the node also returns NotFound (same swallow) → heuristic false → EnsureRunning error. Good, matches test.

But what about a scenario where the holder inspect errors but the node inspect succeeds? Only if the holder name is unresolvable while the node is fine — i.e., holder genuinely deleted. OK.

Now the critical race the PR comment mentions: holder NotFound while node Running — `deployedWithoutNetnsNode` true → `GetNSPath` returns the node's own `/proc/<pid>/ns/net`. That's correct for a shared netns (node joins holder's netns). 

But wait — there's a subtle issue for holder-model nodes whose holder is deleted while the node runs: `GetNSPath` returns the node's ns path — fine. But `Stop` → parks endpoints to parking netns, stops node container. Then `Start`: holder NotFound, node Stopped → fallback → `DefaultNode.Start` → `StartContainer`. But the node container was created with `NetworkMode: container:<holder>`! Reasoning
All confirmed. One thing I should double check: the docstring at `GetNSPath` in `deployedWithoutNetnsNode` mentions "The holder container might not be found yet, when the SR Linux container is Running" — the PR diff shows the comment only as the garbled text. OK.

Now the sros `GetNSPath` legacy gap severity. Actually, let me reconsider whether legacy sros distributed nodes even had `n.netnsNode` initialized under the new code. Yes — `initNetnsNode`/`setupComponentNodes` runs at Init time based on config, so any srsim distributed node running under the new binary has netnsNode non-nil, and `GetNSPath`/`Start` route through the holder regardless of deployment vintage. So legacy srsim labs (deployed by ≤0.79 with components joined to the *base node's* netns? or with a different pause container?) break. Pre-0.80, srsim components used `NetworkMode: container:<base>`? If so, base container holds netns → the same fallback works. The 0.80 note says "components are attached to an internal namespace pause container — the same way Kubernetes holds pod namespaces" implying previously they attached directly to the base node's namespace (or the first component). So the same legacy fallback applies for sros distributed base nodes.

However — I must be careful: is the sros `Stop` in the legacy case broken too? `sros.Stop`: node not Stopped → ParkEndpoints (node's own netns? ParkEndpoints for sros — overrides? The sros `ParkEndpoints` might need netns path — default ParkEndpoints uses parking netns + moves links from node's netns; it uses `ExecFunction`? It uses `d.GetNSPath`?). If Stop works for legacy sros, then Stop parks interfaces; then Start fails → interfaces stuck parked in a named netns; the lab can't be started without recreate. Broken-ish. OK.

Now, is the PR the right place to demand sros parity? The Ponytail rule says a fix must cover all callers of the shared broken mechanism. The shared mechanism is "netns holder lifecycle" — srl and sros both have it. The PR's own comment frames the bug generally ("a node deployed by a containerlab before the holder"). I'll report as P3 with the note that it predates the PR but is the same root cause the PR claims to address; fixing it belongs in the same change (or an immediate follow-up).

Actually, let me double-check whether the sros holder was introduced at the same time as the srl holder in the same commit series — 0.80 vs 0.83 release notes say srsim first (0.80), srl later (0.83). The legacy-sros breakage would have surfaced at 0.80 release time. But maybe sros compat was handled differently — e.g., maybe pre-0.80 srsim deployments are simply unsupported (breaking change documented in 0.80 rn? The note doesn't mention a migration requirement). Let me search 0.80 rn more and sros.go for any pre-0.80 compat handling. Also let me check whether there's any handling for "recreate the node" for sros tests.

  Line 7: [`deploy`](../cmd/deploy.md) now acts like `apply` and converges a running lab to the desired state.   Line 101: - Multi-bind nodes no longer spuriously recreate during deploy/apply reconciliation because bind mount ordering is deterministic. Thanks @FloSch62 #3300


/source/head/docs/rn/0.66.md:
  Line 20: * support for detecting proxy settings when performing `containerlab version upgrade` command #2507


/source/head/docs/rn/0.46.md:
  Line 15:     The `vxlan` link type creates a VXLAN link in the host network namespace and moves it to the node's netns as if this link belongs to the node itself.

  Line 40:     The `vxlan-stitch` mode creates vxlan link in the host netns, but contrary to `vxlan` link type it doesn't move the link to the node's netns; instead it creates a veth link between the node and the host, and uses tc redirect rules to stitch the veth link to the vxlan link.


/source/head/docs/rn/0.11.0.md:
  Line 51: If stopped working when you upgraded to 0.11.0, then re-build the images with vrnetlab 0.2.0


/source/head/docs/rn/0.77.md:
  Line 16: Link changes can be handled live, with a restart, or with a recreate depending on the node kind. Linux, SR Linux, and SR-SIM can apply link changes live; cEOS restarts; vrnetlab-backed and unknown kinds use the conservative recreate mode. You can override this with [`link-apply-mode`](../manual/nodes.md#link-apply-mode) when you have validated that a NOS handles hot-plugged interfaces.


/source/head/docs/rn/0.71.md:
  Line 107: * an alias for the `version upgrade` command has been added - `version update`. #2844


/source/head/docs/rn/0.82.md:
  Line 59: - TX checksum offload management is reapplied on every start for the `cisco_iol` and `linux` kinds. A stop/start cycle recreates the management veth and resets the offload settings to their defaults, which broke TCP/UDP connectivity of IOL nodes. [#3510](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/pull/3510)


/source/head/docs/rn/0.79.md:
  Line 31: The new [`hostname`](../manual/nodes.md#hostname) setting controls the hostname configured inside a node container. It follows the standard node, group, kind, and defaults inheritance order and defaults to the topology node name. Changing a resolved hostname is detected as configuration drift by `deploy`/`apply`, so only the affected node is recreated.


/source/head/docs/rn/0.72.md:
  Line 43: SR-SIM nodes now support [classic CLI mode](../manual/kinds/sros.md#node-configuration) in addition to the existing default Model-Driven mode. This enhancement provides backward compatibility and allows users to validate transition scenarios when the configuration is upgraded from classic CLI to Model-Driven CLI.


/source/head/docs/rn/0.81.md:
  Line 42: The migrated keys participate in the regular node > group > kinds > defaults inheritance, are validated per kind, and are modeled in the JSON schema. Magic variables are resolved in kind-specific config values, as they were in `extras`.

  Line 56: `recreate Pod` entry per affected node, so the preview shows the real lifecycle impact:

  Line 59: │ recreate │ Pod       │ c9s-mv/sros                     │

  Line 66: default: `live` keeps the Pod and gets no entry, while `restart` and `recreate` both replace it and

  Line 67: are reported as `recreate`. When no kind resolver is available the plan degrades to the

  Line 68: conservative recreate default for every affected node, so pod replacements are over-reported


/source/head/docs/rn/0.83.md:
  Line 133: The native VRF setup requires a fresh node container. Export the user configuration before recreating an existing node that uses the previous policy-routing setup; the launcher does not migrate it in place.

  Line 142: Each `nokia_srlinux` node uses an internal `<node-name>-netns` holder container for its network namespace. The holder is hidden from `inspect` unless `--all` is set and is removed with the node. SR Linux nodes now default to the `unless-stopped` restart policy, while an explicitly configured policy is preserved. Nodes with a user-defined `network-mode` keep the previous behavior.

## PR Review: SR Linux compatibility for nodes deployed before the netns holder

### Summary

This PR restores compatibility for SR Linux nodes deployed by containerlab versions before the netns-holder feature: when the holder container is missing while the node container still exists, `srl.Start` and `srl.GetNSPath` now fall back to the node's own network namespace instead of failing with "recreate the node". The change is small, focused, well-placed (a single helper reused by both call sites), and covered by three new mock-runtime tests. I traced all consumers of the changed methods (`apply`/`deploy` reconcile, link deployment, `tools netem`, exec) and found the fallback coherent with `Stop`, `Delete`, and `GetContainers`, which already tolerate a missing holder.

One sibling kind shares the exact holder mechanism and the exact pre-holder deployment scenario but did not get the fallback, and a few smaller polish items remain.

| # | Priority | Finding | Location |
|---|----------|---------|----------|
| 1 | P3 | `nokia_srsim` distributed nodes lack the same pre-holder compatibility fallback | `nodes/sros/sros.go:1827`, `nodes/sros/netns.go:90` |
| 2 | P4 | Garbled comment on `deployedWithoutNetnsNode`; helper is not nil-safe | `nodes/srl/netns.go:117-123` |
| 3 | P4 | Fallback masks the actionable "recreate the node" error when the holder was removed while the node is stopped | `nodes/srl/srl.go:420-434` |
| 4 | P4 | New backward-compatibility behavior is absent from the release notes | `docs/rn/0.83.md:140-145` |

No P0–P2 findings. The core change is correct as written.

### Finding 1 (P3): `nokia_srsim` distributed nodes lack the same pre-holder compatibility fallback

**Location:** [nodes/sros/sros.go L1819-L1842](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/nodes/sros/sros.go#L1819-L1842) and [nodes/sros/netns.go L83-L91](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/nodes/sros/netns.go#L83-L91)

**Problem:** The PR fixes the "node deployed before the holder existed" scenario for `nokia_srlinux`, but the same netns-holder lifecycle exists for `nokia_srsim` distributed base nodes, introduced earlier by the "SR-SIM netns ownership" change (`docs/rn/0.80.md`, "SR-SIM netns ownership"). In `sros.Start`, the distributed-base path calls `n.netnsNode.EnsureRunning(ctx, n.Cfg.ShortName)` unconditionally, and `sros.GetNSPath` returns `n.netnsNode.GetNSPath(ctx)` with no equivalent of `deployedWithoutNetnsNode`.

**Trigger:** A distributed `nokia_srsim` lab deployed by a pre-0.80 containerlab, then managed (`clab start`, stop/start, `tools netem`, link operations) by a binary including this change. `EnsureRunning` fails with "not found; recreate the node" and `GetNSPath` errors, exactly the class of failure this PR fixes for SR Linux.

**Impact:** The stated compatibility goal ("nodes deployed by a containerlab before the holder keep working until it is recreated") is only half fulfilled; users of the sibling kind continue to hit a merge-blocking-style failure that the same fix pattern would resolve. Note one caveat: whether the pre-0.80 srsim netns shape is identical (components joined the base container's netns) could not be verified from this snapshot; if the legacy shape differs, the fallback target needs to be confirmed before porting.

**Suggestion:** Extract the fallback into a shared helper on `NetnsHolder` (for example, a `DeployedWithoutHolder(ctx) bool` check mirroring `deployedWithoutNetnsNode`) and use it in both `srl.Start`/`srl.GetNSPath` and the sros distributed-base paths. If the legacy srsim netns shape turns out to be different, at least keep the kinds consistent by documenting why sros is excluded.

### Finding 2 (P4): Garbled comment on `deployedWithoutNetnsNode`; helper is not nil-safe

**Location:** [nodes/srl/netns.go L117-L123](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/nodes/srl/netns.go#L117-L123)

**Problem:** The comment reads "…it keeps its own network namespace, as a node deployed by a containerlab before the holder does until it is recreated", which is hard to parse. Additionally, the helper dereferences `n.netnsNode` without a guard; both current call sites (`srl.Start` at `srl.go:421` and `GetNSPath` at `netns.go:127`) only avoid the nil dereference through `||` short-circuiting, so a future call site that forgets the guard will panic.

**Trigger:** Any future maintainer reading the helper, or adding a new call site without the nil check.

**Impact:** Misleading documentation and a latent nil-pointer hazard in a small but load-bearing predicate.

**Suggestion:** Rewrite the comment, for example: "reports whether the node keeps its own network namespace: the holder container is missing while the node container still exists, which happens for nodes deployed by a containerlab version before the netns holder; such nodes keep working until they are recreated." Optionally return `false` when `n.netnsNode == nil` inside the helper so it is safe to call unconditionally.

### Finding 3 (P4): Fallback masks the actionable "recreate the node" error when the holder was removed while the node is stopped

**Location:** [nodes/srl/srl.go L420-L434](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/nodes/srl/srl.go#L420-L434)

**Problem:** The status-based heuristic cannot distinguish "legacy node with its own netns" from "holder-model node whose holder container was deleted". In the latter case with the node stopped, the fallback proceeds into `DefaultNode.Start` → `StartContainer` on a container whose `NetworkMode` is `container:<holder>` (`netns.go:96`) with the donor gone. This is inferred from Docker semantics, not measured; the start is expected to fail with a runtime-level error rather than the previous actionable message from `EnsureRunning` ("not found; recreate the node").

**Trigger:** Manual removal (or external cleanup) of the internal `<node>-netns` container while the SR Linux container is stopped, followed by `clab start` or `apply`.

**Impact:** The operation still fails, but the diagnosis degrades from an explicit "recreate the node" instruction to a low-level runtime error. For the running-node case the fallback is a strict improvement (start now succeeds), so this only concerns the error message in the stopped case.

**Suggestion:** In the fallback path, when the node is not running, wrap the `DefaultNode.Start` error (or log a warning when falling back) with a hint that the node may need to be recreated if it was originally deployed with the netns holder. A small log line keeps the working legacy path while preserving diagnosability.

### Finding 4 (P4): New backward-compatibility behavior is absent from the release notes

**Location:** [docs/rn/0.83.md L140-L145](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/47811eb14bae99e1df582747c09f99ccbbe723a2/docs/rn/0.83.md#L140-L145)

**Problem:** The `0.83` release notes describe the netns holder (`docs/rn/0.83.md`, "…uses an internal `<node-name>-netns` holder container…") but do not mention that nodes deployed by earlier releases keep working until recreated. The repository rule for release-note review requires user-visible behavior changes to be reflected in `docs/rn/`; this PR introduces precisely such a change (labs that previously errored on `start` now work).

**Trigger:** A user reading the 0.83 (or next) release notes to understand the holder migration story.

**Impact:** Users cannot tell from the documentation whether upgrading requires recreating SR Linux nodes; the PR's own comment acknowledges recreation is eventually required, which is the part users need to see.

**Suggestion:** Add one sentence to the holder section of the current in-development release note (or the next release note if `0.83` is already published), for example: "SR Linux nodes deployed by earlier releases keep working without a holder; the holder is created when the node is next recreated."

### Coverage notes

- All three changed paths were reviewed in full: `nodes/srl/netns.go`, `nodes/srl/srl.go` (including `Deploy`, `Start`, `Stop`, `Delete`, `GetContainers`), and `nodes/srl/netns_test.go`, plus the base version of `netns.go` to confirm the minimal diff.
- Consumers of the changed methods were traced: `DefaultNode.AddContainerNet` and `ExecFunction` (`nodes/default_node.go:961,999`), `clab tools netem` (`cmd/tools_netem.go:261,548`), and the apply/deploy reconcile flow (`core/topology_reconcile.go`, `core/deploy.go`), confirming an unchanged legacy node is not recreated and link operations use the fallback correctly.
- Runtime semantics verified by source: docker `GetContainerStatus` swallows inspect errors into `NotFound` (`runtime/docker/docker.go:1942-1949`), `DefaultNode.Delete` tolerates `NotFound`, and `postStartActions` refreshes the netns symlink on every start (`runtime/docker/docker.go:1439-1451`).
- No topology/schema changes were made, so `clab.schema.json` was not affected; no CLI help or user docs were changed by this PR beyond the release-note gap in finding 4.
- Tests were not executed (read-only snapshot, execution not permitted); the three added tests were reviewed by inspection and look sound, though the "holder deleted, holder-model node stopped" case from finding 3 is untested.
- Unresolved uncertainties: the exact Docker error when starting a container whose netns donor was removed (inference, finding 3), and the pre-0.80 srsim netns ownership shape (finding 1); both should be verified before acting on the respective suggestions.
- Normal-path performance: the fallback probe adds one extra container inspect per `GetNSPath`/`Start` call (only the holder status; the node status is inspected only when the holder is missing). This is a local, low-cost API call and was not raised as a finding.
